decisions/dec-spatial-pilot.title: Spatial hierarchy qualification direction
decisions/dec-spatial-pilot.content:
Spatial hierarchy qualification direction
Hypothesis, not final selection
Use one coordinate and spatial identity convention, not a universal physical grid. Test a global coarse macro image and spatial index, sparse or compact regional features/pages, deterministic fine terrain, and domain-specific solvers. Start with 4 km macro candidates for the 4,000 km world and compare 1 km and 250 m land/refinement levels. At 256 km, compare the same physical scales and a denser macro source where worthwhile. Do not prescribe all-domain level sizes until actual kernel qualification.
Memory sizing
Illustrative 64 bytes per horizontal cell across a candidate packed field set. This is not measured implementation memory or a claim every field fits. Counts use ceiling division for complete square coverage. Excludes vertical layers, graph links, caches, edits, topology, scratch, snapshots and saves.




































































Spacing (m)256 km cell count64 B/cell4,000 km cell count64 B/cell40004,096256.00 KiB1,000,00061.04 MiB200016,3841.00 MiB4,000,000244.14 MiB100065,5364.00 MiB16,000,000976.56 MiB500262,14416.00 MiB64,000,0003.81 GiB2501,048,57664.00 MiB256,000,00015.26 GiB1006,553,600400.00 MiB1,600,000,00095.37 GiB10655,360,00039.06 GiB160,000,000,0009.31 TiB165,536,000,0003.81 TiB16,000,000,000,000931.32 TiB
A dense 250 m field set across 4,000 km would exceed 15 GiB before any other systems. Dense 1 km costs about 977 MiB even at only 64 B/cell. A 4 km global field is about 61 MiB. This is the reason to avoid hard-coding one resolution for every process. It does not forbid compact, compressed or sparse finer fields with proven budgets.
A 16 km regional page at 250 m contains 4096 cells, costing 256 KiB at 64 B/cell. 1024 such pages cost 256 MiB for that field set, covering 262,144 km², not the whole 4,000 km world. Pages with permanent edits or active storage must remain durably represented even when not resident. Use these values as workload probes, not fixed allocation targets.
Ownership by domain























































DataCandidate authoritative representationDerived consumersGeological baselineVersioned aged macro fields and deterministic regional recipeTerrain, materials, land hydrology, climate priorsSolid geometryFine procedural recipe constrained by durable features, plus committed edits, including cave and structure topologyMesh/collision, storage/face curves, navigation portalsClimate and weatherCoarse horizontal cells and optional vertical state, with conservative exchangesClouds, runoff, radiation, vegetation, wind effectsSoil/landPacked active land/catchment units; optional subgrid cover/soil partitionsRunoff, recharge, evapotranspiration, agricultureRivers/lakes/floodsConnected finite volume stores and geometry-dependent stage/flux relationships; distinct subgrid channels/basinsLocal level/depth/current, navigation hazards, erosionErosionMaterial and sediment budgets plus accepted terrain transactions; aggregate time-integrated forcingsUpdated geography and derived topologyVegetationPersistent cohorts/coverage and durable individual deltas when relevantHarvest, root effects, ET, habitatNavigationVersioned coarse region/portal connectivity and local refined evidenceRoutes, travel times and crowd motionPeople/itemsECS individual identities, finite item/needs state; shared batched activitiesLocal actors and offscreen outcomes
Coarse geometry is not exact fine solid truth; refinement must agree with explicit drainage and passage constraints. A coarse water store can represent many fine locations, but distinct sealed basins cannot share one undifferentiated water level. Use partitions or connectivity-aware features. An aggregate is not a second owner: promote by partitioning amounts and restrict by summing, with appropriate clocks and deterministic/validated reconstruction.
Clock and work scaling
A full linear pass over 16 million 1 km cells every simulated second costs 0.4 CPU seconds/game-second even at an optimistic 25 ns/cell, already 16x the historical 25 ms environment target. For one million 4 km cells the same hypothetical pass costs 25 ms. These are arithmetic examples, not measured performance. Use process-specific intervals, event/due work, compact field layouts and a complete inclusive budget. A severe island-wide storm must not force a fine-cell update everywhere.
First experiment
Use the qualification plan. Compare candidate costs at both world sizes and demonstrate preserved narrow channels and causal offscreen flooding. Final selection requires a measured connected implementation; no runtime launch is authorized by this document.
Source-screened selection update (25 November 2026)
Spatial architecture selection selects a simple global macro field + 16 km regional directory + sparse feature geometry + existing Zylann fine voxel residency for the pilot. The 1 km (256 km world) and approximately 4 km (4,000 km world) macro levels and 250 m regional resolution are comparison settings, not globally imposed. Prioritize the MIT Procedural World Generation donor for CPU channel/valley realization. Regional tributary topology and closed-basin reconciliation are still unresolved. Do not install a second voxel tree or generic AMR runtime. This is a provisional engineering selection; source inspected, not executed or accepted.
Formation review supplement
The same spatial hierarchy can consume either candidate’s exported geography. Formation comparison reopens the macro generator selection and identifies existing deterministic creek growth in Procedural World Generation. No universal grid or second terrain authority is introduced.

environment-stack-pressure-review.title: Integrated environmental foundation pressure review
environment-stack-pressure-review.content:
Integrated environmental foundation pressure review
25 November 2026. Reconciles formation soft lock, integrated decision, sibling review and negative evidence and complementary independent probes. The current user correction supersedes prior native-reuse preference and mesh/sprite-only cloud assumptions. Provisional selection for qualification; no production compatibility, runtime implementation, source build or target benchmark claimed.
Primary and contingency stack


























































































AreaFirst qualificationContingency / residual riskBirth and ageGeoGenesis MIT core, age and geologyPWG whole generator only if soft lock fails and user revisits. No two full formation worlds.MorphologySelected PWG MIT terracing/cliff/mesa/river profile stages; GeoGenesis ProcessPluginExisting deterministic stamp/noise/SDF, same final geometry. No forced 8m cap or decorative creek joins.Regional drainageExtend GeoGenesis seeded priority flood; compare PyFlwDir explicit outlet/length/subgrid kernelsPreserve closed basins and parent spill levels; unresolved fine topology, not inverse IHU.Volume/materialZylann sparse editable SDF, existing noise and persistence; rock properties/prospectivity from GeoGenesisDeterministic cave/ore realization and finite depletion separate gates.LandExisting NOAA CFE candidate, qualify actual native wrapper and clocksWflow SBM or calibrated cheaper reservoir challenger; no duplicate GW.Ordinary downstream flowmizuRoute Apache IRF narrow donor, bounded delay/response storeCompare analytic reservoir and Lagrangian wave; no backwater or false instantaneous arrival.Low-Froude floodWflow MIT local inertia/subgrid donor, SFINCS scientific reference, PyFlwDir geometrySigned diffusive law compare; separate compartments and explicit actual length/sills. Existing native arithmetic comparator only.Steep/rapid hydraulicFluxCell MIT MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC CPU reference then bounded GPU/CPU adaptationClawpack BSD augmented SWE reference; no global fine-grid requirement. If broad fast flows require SWE, qualify coarse shock-capable mode, not suppress them.Aquifers and cave waterSparse finite head/storage, Darcy conductance; Wflow reference and existing native head helpers as comparatorNo CFE conceptual GW double count; bounded sparse implicit solve if stiffness requires. Open caves use connected hydraulic compartments.Atmospheric wind/pressureReduced CPU prognostic hydrostatic/anelastic circulation, Weather3D parent as source leadCompare cheaper diagnostic wind with thermal/pressure forcing (limited fixture) and JCM/SPEEDY reference. No selected validated dynamics; no full browser/GCM runtime.Moisture/cloud/precipMC/TVD conservative transport, CliMA 0M adapted finite cloud and falling phase; CliMT saturation/heatERF Kessler warm rain challenger, not second owner. Snow/ice Wflow HBV solid/liquid stores.Heat/currentsCOARE-informed bulk exchange, cheap slab heat/radiation, wind stress and damped surface velocityRiver Q/A, coastal head partitions if needed; waves visual, no whole ocean CFD.ErosionGeoGenesis implicit stream power, transport-limited/SPACE, hillslope, aeolian donorsActual water/heat/wind/material forcing integrated, bounded edit transactions; no repeated whole age.LiquidsSparse water and second family (lava candidate), distinct mobility/cooling/solidification, basic contaminantViscous shallow flow/reference, not water roughness blind reuse; no full multiphase CFD.Clouds/visualsTrue bounded volumetric raymarch, SunshineClouds2 and Godot-Cloud-Worlds source leadsQuarter-linear resolution, temporal depth-aware reconstruction, shaped density volumes, SDF skip, distant representation only. No stock addon performance claim.Future lifeCohorts/biomass + individual identities; qualify Flecs/EnTT, HPA regional and Recast local, selective DHPA cachesEnvironmental batch queries and hazards; no all-route fine residency or per-tree global simulation.
Formation extensions and current source
GeoGenesis ProcessPlugin receives mutable World, read-only Hydro/Climate/Geology, dt years, returns MassBalance; built-in meteor impact example demonstrates actual extension point. New landforms can be bounded deterministic stages or plugins. Plugins run after built-in chain, so refresh affected hydrology and climate/material descriptors after geometry changes; if intended to age naturally insert initial stage before age. Surface elevation includes sediment (World); do not add loose sediment twice. Fluvial has implicit detachment-limited, transport-limited and SPACE laws; hillslope conservative edge diffusion; aeolian uses simplified prevailing wind. Formation-time drainage estimates not finite runtime flows. At runtime accumulate nonlinear erosion forcing (shear/threshold exposure, not simply mean Q), actual sediment/dust and material removal, commit terrain edits and dirty topology. New caves, overhangs and finite ore require 3D recipe + edited solid state, not surface-height perturbation alone.
GeoGenesis priority flood has seeded/rank-queue and D8/MFD. PyFlwDir provides actual supplied-outlet and unit-catchment routines. Neither magically solves inverse regional refinement. Store parent crossings, outlet and spill elevation, terminal basin identities, feature profiles; resolve cross-window dependencies before claiming exact. Cropping before a remote saddle in independent probe gives false 1m instead of true 5m. Use sparse regional pages/latent constrained features; no all-creek precomputation. 50% land in 4000km square, illustrative drainage density 1km/km² and 100m segments imply 80M segments, 4.77GiB at 64B before links. Aggregate minor headwater response and persist consequential individual feature changes; do not promise exact unseen local state if only aggregate known.
Published implementation c7b4ede9af45a67a6ddd3d65cd5685d3af79c320: native flux already contains local inertia and conservative exchanges; groundwater head/conductance/SPD; air face transport, morphology, soil exchange useful existing evidence but no reuse preference. Historical Flood078 1124 CPU-ms/game-s vs 25 target; earlier SWMM/CaMa failures; no revival of old LandscapeChannels/preparation, no broad legacy API/save compatibility. Compare narrow primitives only under same acceptance gates. Local unpublished code not inspected. Aokana paper’s explicit lack of runtime voxel edits prevents replacement of Zylann based solely on rendering benchmark.
Shared authority and coupling


















































OwnerDurable quantity / geometryInputs and outputsTerrainversioned aged baseline, deterministic recipe, committed solid/material editsbed/crest/profile, slope, roughness, cave void and portal revisions; accepts erosion/structuresSurfaceone water stock per connected partition/reach, constituent, momentum or delayed release representationstage-volume inversion, Q/A and flood duration, actual ET/recharge/withdrawal, sedimentsSoilCFE root-zone, queues/interception, snow and recharge pendingexact areal precipitation, actual ET and runoff/recharge; remove conceptual GW if spatial owner receives rechargeGWfinite aquifer/cave stock, headDarcy exchange, seepage, springs/extraction, geometry revisionsAtmospheredry/moist air mass convention, energy/temp, pressure/wind, vapor/cloud/falling liquid/iceactual vapor/heat and rain transfer, cloud state, solar/season/wind fieldsSediment/materialloose/mobile/deposited solid and dust/sinksactual integrated forcing, bounded solid edits; retain finite material accountEcologyregional biomass/cohort, durable individual deltassoil/radiation/thermal/wetness/hazards; roots/roughness/infiltration/actual ET feedbackECS/nav/renderentity identity/state; derived portals and render buffersbatched field queries and invalidation; never second physical owner
16km page directory, common checked metric coordinates, independent solver lattices. 256km macro 1km; 4000km macro 4km; 250m regional only conditional on actual geometry/accuracy. Use compact SoA, direct page directory, stable IDs, sparse graph; keep no dense 1m world. Overlap area/contacts precomputed once per geometry revision; transfer amounts by actual integrated interval. CFE m per step and timestep_h/time_step_size: convert by catchment area and actual seconds. Its total includes conceptual GW/runoff; partition/replace conceptual GW if external spatial solver. Potential ET is not actual atmospheric credit. Atmospheric mixing ratio not mass; flux-consistent dry-air convention and explicit heat. Transfer water kg or m³ with explicit density, do not reuse same numeric value in different units. f64 or compensated partitioned amounts: f32 ocean 8e15m³ loses 100m³ update, ULP ~537M m³. Local intensive f32 only with measured error.
Scheduler: atmosphere/land supplies ET demand, water donor accepts finite actual quantity and energy, face-advection, saturation/heat, finite cloud removal into falling precipitation, below-cloud evaporation, actual precipitation split by area, snow melt/refreeze, CFE infiltration/runoff/recharge, surface/GW routing, integrated erosion, revisioned terrain transactions. Each owner tracks completed physical horizon and pending amount, no duplicate credits on retries or applying future rain early. Bulk interval arrays not per-face/per-entity messages. Different stable step sizes reconcile one boundary transfer, not global smallest dt. Promotion/restriction moves stock and delayed history, parent summary becomes derived, no duplicate quantity. Terrain edit invalidates geometry and dependent topology; barrier closure effective before next relevant transfer, affected-basin repair may propagate nonlocally. Queries current/coarse/pending/stale explicitly labeled. Save/restart stocks, clocks, topology and pending exchanges.
Hydraulic method limits and pressure results
Ordinary reach IRF uses normalized response weights and finite transit queue; source mizuRoute conv_upsbas_qr has volume and future flow, clamp and shift, short-length branch resetting stock. Qualify exact remaining inventory, cap/withdrawal, delayed release and re-route when topology changes. Do not count queue and reach volume twice or lose capped release. Promote downstream shortcut to signed head mode before backwater/overflow/control matters; do not run both simultaneously over same water. Local inertia Qnew=(Qold+gAdt(etaA-etaB)/L)/(1+gdtn²abs(Qold)/(R^(4/3)*A)). Need monotone connected V(stage), face area/conveyance/sill/actual path length; no bathtub flood. Quasi-steady diffusive signed Manning challenger for slow flows. Use applicable control/rating laws or full shallow-water momentum for rapid falls/dam breaks. Sibling 1m dam-break local inertia normalized L1 ~40%, HLL 2.64% with exact ledger: local inertia not universal. FluxCell actual MIT source has HLLC, hydrostatic reconstruction, scalar and CPU reference; author 610–700M updates/s preprint not peer-reviewed nor local benchmark. Editable bed retains depth, solid mask fixed, GPU batches/readbacks/ownership need qualification; no full-island 1m solver.
Complementary actual independent C++20 O3 single thread virtual EPYC 9V74, 100x100km synthetic all-active rectangle, closed boundaries, 100mm/h x1h, piecewise volume and rectangular face, no true geometry/land/air/save/render. 1km/30s: 0.025300 CPU-ms/physical-s. 250m/30s: 0.383678; 250m/10s: 1.179750; 250m initially 5m/10s: 1.150764. 30.72MB arrays at 250m, max residual relative to initial+rain 3.42e-13. Fixed dt not certified. Tests stage inverse, no incoming below crest, reversal after momentum reset, simultaneous donor cap and gate; deliberately oversized 2-cell step oscillates 1->0 vs equilibrium 0.5 despite conserving water. Need finer actual reference, real geometry and timestep convergence.
Atmosphere and volumetric clouds
Weather3D parent hydrostatic anelastic C-grid 12 layers RK3, pressure projection each stage with DFT/Thomas and iterative terrain correction. Source includes Earth steering and internal moisture/soil clamps; no whole adoption. Compare 32/16km 8-layer reduced prognostic first, 4 layers only if storm/vertical accuracy passes, regional 8km/parameterized narrow convection. Cheap evolving diagnostic wind/heat benchmark control is not full weather. Need evolving pressure/wind, vertical exchange, terrain uplift/rain shadow, saturation and latent heat, seasonal/diurnal forcing, finite moisture. CliMT C-binding column physics is alternative reference with independent condensation/mixing/surface switches, JCM SPEEDY independent 8-level reference, COARE bulk exchange. CliMA 0M threshold relaxation analytic fixed-excess removal, adapt actual phase/fall-delay; ERF Kessler warm rain challenger. HBV snowpack solid/liquid degree-day melt/refreeze with actual stock and liquid retention; ice/heat approximations explicit. Weather and plant fields include wind direction/speed, humidity/temp, radiation, precipitation and wetness. Rivers velocity Q/A, wind-driven damped slab current for lakes/ocean, optional Coriolis; coastal storage/flow if surge impacts gameplay; no separate decorative physical water authority.
Independent constant-wind tracer 4000km 1D periodic, Gaussian sigma64km, 720km translation, CFL.1: 32km first-order L1 82.53% vs MC21.28%; 16km 59.22% vs6.95%; 8km39.06% vs1.91%. Both mass errors <1e-15. Varying velocity ordinary interpolation loses 3.53% in separate toy example, not Weather3D measurement. Sibling tests include narrow sigma12km: even 8km MC inadequate for tested threshold; subgrid convection or refine where needed. Sibling AVX2 four-scalar 16km 8-layer transport median 2.764ms/step only, no pressure/vertical/etc. Prefer MC/TVD, not upwind-only; validate actual multi-D flux-consistent mass and thermal dynamics.
True volumetric clouds mandatory. Sibling record source-reviewed SunshineClouds2 (MIT Godot compositor) and Godot-Cloud-Worlds (MIT SDF skipping). Test actual bounded 3D density shape volumes driven by atmospheric cloud mass/height/coverage and wind, 480x270 at 1080p, 24–48 primary steps, cheap light, empty-space skip, depth-aware temporal history/rejection. 32 primary steps all-screen 4.147M samples vs 132.71M full-HD/64; not GPU benchmark, nested lights and overlapping volumes can dominate. Eight 128³ R8 volumes 16MiB before mips; share cloud shape assets, not per-cloud grids. True local/fly-through density, distant sky cached if consistent, no sprite-only substitution. Weather determines amount/form and motion, visuals do not own moisture. Test above/inside/below, storm/dawn/night, depth edges, motion and time acceleration on RTX2070S. No measured GPU result.
Performance pressure and clocks
4000km: 16km page directory 62,500 x32B=1.91MiB; macro4km 1M x64B=61MiB; 1km 16M x64B=977MiB; 250m 256M x64B=15.26GiB. 32km atmospheric columns 15,625 x8=125k layer cells x64B=7.63MiB; 16km30.52MiB; 8km122.07MiB. Snapshots/face/pressure/geometry/stock/scratch excluded. At 8x, 25 CPU-ms/game-s=.2 CPU core average, ~3.33 CPU-ms/frame across workers at 60fps; at 64x 1.6 cores, ~26.67 CPU-ms/frame total, not main thread. Broad storms must not expand all fine regions. Hypothetical dense 1M surface cells at synthetic probe stride ~192MB before subgrid tables. Do not extrapolate as real performance.
Default day600 game seconds vs literal86400 physical seconds implies factor144. Independent 250m/30s cost becomes55.25 CPU-ms/game-s, 10s169.88, deep165.71 before others. Freeze explicit common coupled environment seconds/game second, qualify 1,10,144 and gameplay pacing. 1:1 is not accepted final time scale (1 physical hour spans 6 game days); calendar/solar forcing and geological years distinct. Don’t speed rain/ET alone or hide time multiplier. CFL includes effective storage/face dimensions and pressure/vertical stability; no arbitrary long step based on cheap mass-only check.
Bounded gate and Codex brief
No final technology lock beyond user’s terrain soft lock. High risks: actual refined topology/geometry without fine-world preprocessing; regime switching and stable subgrid flood accuracy; real reduced circulation plus mixed-phase heat; global physical/game-time pacing; true cloud GPU cost. Full compatibility designed, not validated. Proposed tolerances before tests: topology/closed barriers hard pass, compare stage/arrival and extent with independent finer reference (initial example extent IoU>=.85, arrival within 10% or one coarse step, relevant stage error <=.1m or 10% depth; select scenario thresholds before execution). Normalize conservation by transferred amount/local balance as well as world inventory. 

~1.5h work allocation: pin actual checkout, build GeoGenesis single-shot age/export, explicit original/filled fields, 256km macro and 4000km macro timing separately. No dense fine generation. If build fails, labeled known-answer fixture only, not natural baseline success.
~1.5h: bounded region plus adjacent seam, shared outlet/closed basin, selected PWG landform and Zylann render; compare repeat/reload and exact geometry/cave if possible.
~2h: qualify mizuRoute-type IRF (finite pending/withdrawal/promotion), Wflow-type subgrid head transport and FluxCell CPU reference on known-answer dam/levee/arrival. Do not require successful wholesale port. Compare native only same criteria, no preference. 
~2h: actual CFE donor and finite rain/ET/heat, MC transport, reduced wind/pressure donor or explicit limited control; test downwind rain, cloud phase and snow; no claim full atmosphere if prescribed. 
~1h: normal host connected small natural terrain/water/weather, terrain edit and save/reload, actual visuals (true volumetric cloud smoke test if feasible), offscreen, inclusive costs and exact blockers. Subsequent whole-island actual storm, long-distance travel and population gate, not accepted on toy data.
This is a bounded one-day qualification proposal, not a promise to finish all systems in one day. Codex: read accepted Brain records and pinned source, one writer, separate scratch lineage; retain Godot/Jolt/Zylann, no LandscapeChannels, no whole app transplant, no new scheduler/voxel tree by default. Follow gates, record actual commands/source/binary, CPU/game and physical seconds, GPU/RAM/VRAM, init/prep/rebuild, visual result, failures and remaining uncertainty. User authorization needed for game runtime changes; no main merge here.

environmental-foundation-v1-environment-.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — fast environmental development and continuous terrain LOD
environmental-foundation-v1-environment-.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — fast environmental development and continuous terrain LOD
27 November 2026. User-approved active execution plan. This supersedes prior scene-first, colony-based, and mandatory showcase interpretations. Previous exact delivery plan. The technical plan remains the selected numerical and architectural baseline; execution protocol governs delivery. No new implementation or performance claim is made by this authorization.
Binding scope and authority
One permanent, reusable environment-only development baseline for Codex, not a user-facing application. Native C++/headless execution is preferred for numerical work when cheaper; use the same underlying V1 owners and at most one active Godot environmental development scene for rendering, streaming and integration. UI is optional and not a deliverable. Reuse existing code and artifacts, never create a new scene or simulation for each test. No colonist creation, ticks, walking, scheduling, navigation/settlement work, benchmarking, optimization or compatibility work in this scope. Colonists will be revisited separately; preserve existing unrelated source and saves, not their current implementation as a requirement.
The user and planning chat own substantive architecture decisions through the canonical Brain. Codex follows the selected stack, requirements and contracts; it may make bounded implementation fixes, dependency-aware build changes, safe caches and reversible configuration choices within that design. Do not reopen solver/renderer selection, replace Zylann, change authoritative ownership, physical clocks, requirements, major dependencies, or scope without explicit user approval. Report an evidenced fundamental blocker and a concrete recommendation; continue independent in-scope work.
Retain GeoGenesis, selected PWG methods, Zylann, Wflow-derived water and groundwater, NOAA CFE, FluxCell, MeanderPy, Weather3D-derived circulation, CliMA phase physics, COARE-derived exchange and SunshineClouds2 as selected in the technical plan. Keep independent spatial/temporal granularity, 1:1 coupled physical clock, finite water/heat/sediment custody, current editable geometry, offscreen consequences, and attractive eventually scalable rendering. No second production solver or terrain authority. No forced backward compatibility with obsolete colony, save or environment mechanisms. Environmental field/geometry query contracts remain; do not implement or qualify their colony consumers now.
Source audit and current bottlenecks
Read actual implementation at a891cc78, canonical Brain at 70b671f6 (prior delivery plan) and published mirror at 91ce97f0 (source revision 367d3ad). Public mirror is behind; use latest canonical records. Progress, terrain, water, weather. The numerical core is connected; remaining general water/terrain contacts, broad recession, natural morphology, weather structure and visual/performance acceptance still open. Latest reviewed code includes finite ground heat thaw of snow; do not infer validation from commit alone.

build.ps1 recompiles Rust core/exporter, five C units, ten C++ units and the pilot into new output. Third-party source cache already exists, but compiled-unit reuse does not appear in that path. run_preview.ps1 stages a fresh isolated project and save; its earlier single-pilot restrictions are not the desired production test workflow. Preserve exact build identity, dependency/license pins, scratch isolation and guard policies. Reuse unchanged compiled units and prepared project/shader imports using existing build tooling, a minimal incremental path or an existing dependency-aware build system if one already fits. Never run stale binaries or overwrite a running addon. Skip unrelated gameplay full rebuilds.
Existing atlas and atlas capture entry already provide field selection, raster presentation and inspection, but depend on previous simulation packet APIs and some fixed old semantics. Reuse simple raster/stroke/presentation pieces only if cheaper than a compact exporter. Do not port legacy hydraulic ownership, old atlas validation campaigns or require a large new UI. Native V1 recipe, network, flood, land, weather and cloud queries exist in binding. Export selected accepted fields in batches from current owners; no per-pixel Godot calls or full-resolution voxel scan.
Terrain binding configures four LODs, 32-voxel mesh blocks, 64m primary/secondary LOD distance, normally 512m view distance, 1760m island-overview metadata option, disabled LOD fade, disabled generated-block caching and GPU generation, enabled LOD0 collision, disabled normal maps and terrain shadow casting. Coarsest voxel spacing is 8m, mesh block span 256m. These settings are inherited, not qualified optimal for V1. Generator allocates and writes three full channel arrays per block, samples X/Z once per column, then iterates every Y. It has no explicit uniform-block early-out. Terrain sampler bilinearly interpolates macro bed/material fields; carving already bounds candidate reach search to neighboring macro cells. Avoid misdiagnosing a global channel scan. Potential cost: repeated X/Z evaluation across vertical blocks, full air/solid fills, array allocation/copy, stream/mesher/main-thread/collision work, LOD admission. Potential appearance: coarse source interpolation, narrow features undersampled, transitions/material shading/fade, missing far mesh coverage. Hypotheses, not measured causes. Earlier M1 reports plain coarse surface with visible creases; 452ms stream with 3,935 generated calls/326 mesh blocks; subsequent material run 1.933s local stream, 1,358 callbacks, 200 mesh blocks, cold local stream 132ms. Different fixtures, not comparable timing trend. Do not confuse fast formation exporter with visible terrain readiness.
Latest 4,000km trial evidence used 1M formation cells, 35,907 catchments, 171,351 flood compartments and 4,096 air columns at 62.5km. Reopened +100 physical seconds in 22.55s (4.43x) with actors; not environment-only target measurement. Routine small development must not use this setup. World weather target spacing is currently 8km and maximum side bounded (64 in recorded macro). Small weather cases require configurable resolution or enough columns; no meaningless 2x2/4x4 storm claim.

A. Make iteration fast — first implementation package

Inventory existing V1 build/preview/pilot/session entry paths and actual checkout instructions. Consolidate them into one reusable, scriptable environment baseline, not another application. Start from terrain_v1_session.gd, existing native surface-water pilot and current V1 native owners. Extract useful existing scenario and rendering code without duplicating physical initialization, clocks, edits, save or repair logic. Native-only numerical mode, headless integration mode and rendered mode are execution choices of this baseline. Use at most one active Godot environment scene, only when needed. Keep historical scenes/receipts as evidence; no unrelated cleanup or wholesale scene rewrite. No requirement for a UI, manual controls or an editor product.
Extend existing build tooling with dependency-aware reuse of Rust core/exporter, C/C++ object files, pinned third-party inputs and addon link outputs. No compiler invocation for unchanged compatible inputs; rebuild only affected translation units and dependent links. Key by actual source/header dependency, compiler/flags, toolchain, upstream pin and build identity, not timestamp or blanket commit hash alone. Keep exact receipts and workload guard. Never reuse stale binaries or overwrite a loaded addon. Script-only changes should not rebuild native code. Reuse staged Godot project/import cache when compatible; update changed files only.
Generate and age one primary reusable world recipe (prefer existing 64x48km seed 713 if its geography is suitable; 64km-class alternative if not). Keep an immutable compatible initial checkpoint and cheap isolated scratch state for each scenario; reuse actual artifacts across runs and reset only mutable state. Recipe cache includes generation settings/seed/dimensions, generation dependencies and schema; checkpoint additionally includes actual state/owner compatibility and physical settings. Do not invalidate recipes because unrelated solver or UI code changed. Do not force incompatible checkpoints or create migrations just to reuse them. Regenerate only affected artifacts on explicit request or relevant dependency change. Keep single writer, guarded execution and private saves protected.
One command/runner entry for the common development loop; select mode, world/checkpoint, scenario, physical horizon, settings and diagnostic output as necessary. It should be usable by Codex without human UI interaction. Reuse existing native queries/exporters and minimal scripts; do not build a large harness, generic debug platform or editor. Do not instantiate colony services or depend on a colony quantum/actor clock; advance the same accepted environmental physical time with environmental owners. For geometry-dependent tests, use real current terrain and edit paths, not a fake numerical substitute.
Demonstrate reuse once with concise cold/warm timing and identities: unchanged invocation reuses compiled artifacts, recipe, prepared workspace and checkpoint; a relevant source change rebuilds only dependencies; changed generation inputs invalidate the recipe; mutable runs leave baseline unchanged. Confirm zero actor workload, no stale artifacts, and meaningful accepted simulation results. Record measured wall time per preparation/build/open/run/diagnostic phase where useful. Avoid an elaborate validation matrix. Proceed immediately to B.

Use the primary world for ordinary integration. Small bounded/native fixtures only when they are cheaper or expose a specific invariant; 128km or finer weather spacing only when a meaningful storm/topology requires it. 512km only for a meaningful scale question; 4,000km only for major continent-rendering/scale acceptance or a specific blocker. Cache compatible larger recipes/checkpoints. These sizes are proposed working presets, not mandatory suites, fixed caps or new physical requirements.
B. Terrain loading and smooth continent-to-ground rendering — priority after A
User requires extremely smooth LODs, rapid continuous zoom from a full continent through regional views to local editable terrain, without loading exponentially more fine voxels. Achieve this with minimal architectural change and existing Zylann/Transvoxel functionality wherever feasible. A whole-continent 2D atlas or logical world size alone is not proof of this 3D requirement.

On the same reusable high-relief/channel-bearing location, measure cold/warm first coarse visible terrain, first usable local detail, convergence and rapid zoom/flyover. Separate formation/export, recipe/hydrography admission, generator work, stream/mesh/transfer/main thread/collision and GPU costs. Use existing counters and timing, selected near/mid/far material and LOD/wireframe captures, intermediate frames and visible readiness; do not assume a cause from source alone. The earlier continent-style lab had six LODs, local 1,024m view and a separate macro chart, not continuous whole-domain 3D. Reuse relevant existing code only; do not revive its old geography authority.
Fix dominant measured generation/streaming bottlenecks in a coherent batch. Evaluate uniform air/solid fast paths, repeated X/Z work across vertical blocks, allocation/copy and bounded caches only where profile supports them. Preserve SDF/material semantics, cave/overhangs, edits, borders and actual hydraulic geometry. Reuse upstream controls. Tune configurable LOD count, distance/error, transition/fade, cache/GPU options, collision and viewer demand according to actual measurements; do not blindly raise global draw distance or fine voxel count.
Keep a usable coarser representation resident until required finer coverage is ready; prioritize destination refinement, bound/cancel stale requests where supported, avoid visible holes, cracks, popping, z-fighting and large transient allocations. Use existing world-coordinate/rebase conventions for large distances. Keep collision and fine generation local or physically requested, not continent-wide. Camera only controls presentation; simulation and physical state remain independent.
If measured existing Zylann coverage is inadequate at continent/mid-scale, use the cheapest necessary derived coarse surface/mesh hierarchy from the same current recipe plus revisioned edit/morphology summaries. Reuse existing raster/mesh/paging pieces when suitable. Select detail by projected error/coverage; use bounded residency and localized invalidation; preserve shared coast/river/landform placement and continuity when handing off to near Zylann meshes. This is a conditional small presentation adapter, not a second solid world, new renderer project, SVDAG migration or solver redesign. If it requires a fundamental renderer or ownership change, report blocker for user decision before proceeding with that change.
Verify one normal near/mid/far sequence and a cached continent-scale zoom at meaningful terrain acceptance, not every subsequent package. Show actual Godot 3D, stable coverage and transitions, bounded working-set/queue costs, current edits agreeing with near and relevant coarse data, and measured first-visible/usable latency and frame/memory costs. Compare like-for-like against the initial baseline. Do not invent a fixed timing target absent agreement; improve demonstrated major bottlenecks and report remaining defects. Keep eventually attractive shading, geology and recognizable terrain; no camera-driven changes to physical state. A 2D atlas remains a cheap independent diagnostic.

C. Complete connected water (M2)
Finish remaining actual regional functionality: natural finite connected rivers, lakes, ocean, coarse catchment runoff and aquifers/springs/cave outlets; independent flood compartments and broad rise/return/recession; supported split/edited geometry and barriers; automatic rapid-flow custody/return using existing FluxCell, correct finite water/tracer/heat transfers and current terrain repair. Generalize owning records and meaningful contacts rather than duplicate isolated pilots. Keep water queries and derived stage/depth/velocity/hazard fields, not navigation or colony integration. Use actual connected water on the primary world with a cheap stage/discharge/flood-depth map and hydrograph or bounded control where appropriate. Demonstrate no water creation or loss, no crossing sealed barriers, meaningful downstream/offscreen consequences, and recession/retained stock as physically applicable. Do not force all basins dry. Render visible water only for relevant appearance/geometry work. No unnecessary Godot launch, full-world birth or full test suite.
D. Complete atmosphere and coupled surface exchange (M3)
Finish sustained circulation, meaningful regional storms/topography response, rain/snow transport, cold/warm finite evaporation/heat and atmosphere/land/water feedback. Use the existing selected methods and common accepted clock, not a new climate model. Correct incomplete regional coverage, weather resolution and physically eligible cold-air/open-water exchange as needed; preserve actual mass and energy, falling phase and queue custody. Use the primary world with suitable configurable grid or larger domain only if needed to demonstrate meaningful spatial structure. Show actual humidity/rain/snow/temperature/wind/condensate fields, vertical section or temporal curves; use Godot only for actual volumetric cloud appearance or relevant integration. No artificial visual rain owning water, duplicate atmospheric simulation or arbitrary forcing to hide missing physics.
E. Complete living terrain evolution (M4)
Complete actual accumulated-flow/weather-driven erosion, finite sediment transport, downstream settling/deposition and natural alluvial migration/cutoffs using existing GeoGenesis-derived methods and selected MeanderPy calculations. Respect materials, real geometry/barriers and finite stocks; apply bounded persistent current-geometry transactions and repair dependent hydraulic summaries/visuals. Do not merely move visual splines or recarve from stage. Compare actual bed/centerline/material change and sediment accounting over appropriate forcing; use the same reusable environment and only additional focused checks needed for changed behavior.
F. Integrated environmental qualification (M5)
Finish the combined terrain/water/weather/evolution with actual offscreen progression, real current edits and persistent coherent state, attractive representative 3D terrain/water/clouds and the required whole-continent-to-local rendering capability. Demonstrate one representative severe regional storm/recession (technical plan 100x100km), and meaningful 4,000km macro plus multiple active environmental regions using cached recipes and bounded residency; use 512km intermediate only if useful. Do not require a separate run on every preset. Measure actual accepted environment-only throughput against 8x and 60 FPS reference goal for representative rendered work; record CPU/GPU, RAM/VRAM, p95/p99, debt and active workload counts as relevant, not idle macro alone. 32x stretch and all colony/entity work are deferred. Reopen checks only for changed persistence or representative integrated acceptance. Do not claim validation for unmeasured or unresolved behavior. Continue independent packages if a blocker needs user decision; no routine pause at milestones.
Diagnostic selection
Use the cheapest representation that directly demonstrates the changed capability. Actual data only, clear units, legend/scale, seed/region and accepted physical timestamp, consistent color range for comparisons. A coarse image is acceptable; interpolation/visual-only enhancement must be labeled. Export one relevant layer or a small set, not every field continuously. Mark unknown/stale/pending distinctly. Diagnostic refresh never drives physics or forces fine terrain residency. Prefer existing raster/atlas pieces, simple batch image/CSV output and actual Godot views when appropriate. For a loading defect include intermediate frames and readiness timeline, not only a final loaded screenshot. For a solver change include meaningful fields and mass/energy sanity, not a generic screenshot. Whole island overview is useful for macro terrain and network topology but not required elsewhere. Do not block implementation on building a comprehensive debugging UI or producing videos.
No new test execution, runtime changes or definitive terrain diagnosis by this plan. Report each substantial package with exact commits and concise directly relevant measurements/diagnostics, unresolved limits and next work. Update canonical Brain at meaningful checkpoints, not every microchange. Previous physics and performance evidence retains its scope; current code and actual new measurements establish progress.
27 November 2026 — controlling completion campaign and reusable demonstrations
User approves a fresh local Codex campaign to finish V1 from the existing implementation, not restart it. At planning review the pushed runtime was 75b7520a, the canonical Brain was 97c45754 and the generated mirror’s source marker matched. Fetch actual latest heads and inspect local ownership before assigning work. All accepted physical requirements, selected technologies, environment-only scope and 1:1 physical/game clock remain binding. No colonists, ECS/population, navigation, settlement, unrelated cleanup or compatibility work. Do not reopen completed technology choices.
Remaining packages and completion boundaries
A is already verified; retain its single guarded runner, dependency-aware compilation, compatible immutable recipes/checkpoints and prepared Godot workspace. Extend only the minimal existing command interface. The following two lanes are a concrete closure sequence for B–F and outstanding M1 functionality. They can proceed concurrently where independent, then converge on F. The owner of a shared file/contract or integrated build is assigned explicitly; never have two writers in one worktree.













































PackageOwner / dependencyRequired finished functionality and reusable demonstrationB1 Formation and agingTerrain/render workerExpose geological age, aging step and selected formation settings through the existing runner, without changing GeoGenesis/PWG selection or fixed valid physical semantics. Show genuinely progressive birth/aging snapshots from the same seed/formation history (not unrelated regenerated worlds or a visual morph). Use existing upstream step/export capability or inexpensive cached equivalent stages only after verifying equivalence. Cache recipes and requested sparse stages, label actual elapsed geological years. Maintain real drainage/channel/basin/material geometry including representative tributaries and curves; final snapshot feeds the same current-terrain and physical owners. Provide an optional configurable distant 3D aging playback in the shared scene, and cheap elevation/drainage/change fields. Verify that different ages change actual terrain, same inputs reproduce it, and replay does not recompute completed compatible stages.B2 Standard streaming, LOD and terrain qualityTerrain/render worker, after B1 or its independent setupIntegrate the existing measured bounded Zylann clipbox change into the ordinary pinned, reproducible V1 engine build (with tested fallback/debug controls), not only an isolated editor-flight DLL. Separate presentation demand from data-only edit/save leases; keep coarse coverage while refining, bound queued changes, preserve current edits and parent consistency. User reports that whole-island views look poor and detail loads too slowly. Improve actual large-scale landform/coast/channel composition and regional/local continuity, not just numerical probe counts. Inspect real near/mid/far images at matching poses, optimize the significant visual and streaming bottlenecks, tune configurable LOD distances/count/coarsest allowed level, and document suitable defaults and supported camera movement speeds. Measure fixed-pose first coarse/usable/fine readiness plus a reproducible continuous fly/zoom route, with a genuinely faster route only if needed to establish a useful operating envelope. Do not hide loading by slowing the test camera, disabling physical work, or extending a hold. Test manual inspection of a chosen LOD as a display-only option. One representative 4,000 km route and local edit are enough for package qualification; use cached state. Preserve 3D quality and bounded memory rather than adding global fine voxels. If existing hierarchy proves insufficient, the previously authorized derived coarse presentation handoff remains conditional, not a new terrain engine.C1 General connected waterPhysical-systems workerExtend the existing revisioned finite water/terrain/land/air geometry repair paths beyond the demonstrated one-owner cases: meaningful lateral cave inflow/outflow, shoreline partial/reverse/adjacent/multiple edits and connected receiver changes, barriers, dams/weirs/gates, extraction, flooding and recession. Prioritize general physical mechanisms over searching repeatedly for rare locations; use a controlled representative real editable geometry when natural examples are scarce. Preserve finite stocks and pending parcels, no flow through sealed terrain, safe atomic revision updates, local edits and offscreen outcomes. Do not implement colony consumers. Provide a configurable water test: storm/river/lake/flood scenario with an optional actual barrier/edit/withdrawal, native depth/velocity/stock/hydrograph maps and an optional advancing 3D view showing stages and recession. Reuse the current supported physical cases rather than recertifying each historical pilot.C2 Adaptive detailed waterPhysical-systems worker, within CReplace the verified single active fine-flood slot with bounded configurable concurrent fine patches using existing FluxCell/parent transfers. Generalize admission, hysteresis, release after edited rapid flow, mixed-phase/heat/tracer handling and safe overlapping or neighboring custody without duplicate volume. Keep detail physical and sparse, not camera-driven. Demonstrate multiple simultaneously necessary regions, conservative exchanges, release/reuse, and continued coarse behavior outside the active detail. Use a finite representative forcing/edit on current terrain, not dense global fine grids or arbitrary fixed cap hiding important rapid flow; report unsupported scale honestly. Combine with C1’s reusable water scenario rather than a separate Godot scene.D Coupled weather and readable moving cloudsPhysical-systems worker owns physical weather; terrain/render worker owns presentation, after B2; coordinate snapshot interface onceClose remaining physical weather requirements using existing Weather3D/CliMA/COARE methods: meaningful terrain-driven winds, wet/dry regions and mountain rain shadow, advected cloud/precipitation, finite snow/ice, evaporation/condensation, heat, drought/rewetting, and actual feedback to/from land/water with declared boundary/solar forcing. Reuse working coupled dynamics; do not rebuild it or invent artificial rain. For presentation fix the unresolved moving-cloud signal 11 failure, retire diagnostic-only workarounds when normal rendering can use the same verified mechanism, and achieve distinct moving volumetric cloud formations/clear gaps when physical conditions permit, consistent depth/light over terrain/water and attractive regional views. Use a reproducible advancing weather scenario with matching accepted-time weather atlas: select layer/height, temperature, wind vectors, humidity, condensate/cloud coverage, rain/snow and surface fields where available. Export existing WeatherFields/native data in batches and reuse lightweight atlas/raster presentation; no new UI requirement. Show actual cloud movement and physical fields evolving together; a fixed still or arbitrary shader animation alone is insufficient. One regional native time sequence and relevant rendered moving view, not repeated shader micro-tuning.E Living terrainPhysical-systems worker after C topology; use shared terrain owner, renderer worker assists only at defined integration boundariesGeneralize actual accumulated-flow/rainfall/material-driven erosion, settling and deposition across current terrain; complete wider alluvial migration, moving sections and natural cutoff/shortcut with residual oxbow and finite water/heat/sediment/connectivity. Reuse selected GeoGenesis/MeanderPy methods and common revision transactions. If natural generated cases lack a neck, choose a suitable representative geometry/forcing using the same production mechanism; do not fabricate a successful cutoff by manually drawing one. Support offscreen evolution. Reusable evolving-river test shows actual before/after or time sequence of bed, centerline, sediment and flood response (optional fixed-camera time-lapse), with material/water accounting and meaningful downstream consequences.F Release integrationOrchestrator after both lanes, delegate bounded final fixesMake the existing V1 environmental path the ordinary fresh-world foundation, with obsolete environmental paths disconnected when safe; no colony consumer changes. Run one combined representative 100 km severe storm with flooding/recession, current edit, physical weather/erosion and save/reopen, and one cached 4,000 km advancing full 3D zoom/flyover with meaningful offscreen active regions and bounded terrain/solver residency. Reuse package tests where applicable instead of rerunning a matrix. Show actual accepted water, weather and terrain advancing together, coherent local edits and persistent state, representative attractive near/mid/far images and matching fields, no normal-run crash. Report 8x/60 FPS reference performance honestly on existing target hardware including frame distribution, worst stalls, RAM/VRAM, queue/debt and active workload. Do not spend repeated runs optimizing insignificant deviations (e.g. 59.964 vs 60 FPS) while a substantive feature is missing; report exact results and address meaningful defects. Do not infer broad active-flood macro qualification from dry macro or single patch. Finish and stop when accepted full V1 scope is implemented and representative checks meet the agreed requirements; report actual remaining blockers rather than expanding V1. 32x stretch and all colony work remain deferred.
The technical plan and original physical contracts remain requirements. The table specifies remaining completion work, not permission to drop unlisted accepted capabilities. Existing verified evidence remains valid within its original scope. Inspect only the relevant code and evidence before each package; do not repeat research/benchmark campaigns that have already delivered their answer.
One reusable command-driven demonstration contract
Extend develop.ps1, the existing shared terrain/environment session, native field exporters and existing flight code. The GeoGenesis exporter already accepts age and step; develop.ps1 currently uses 40,000 and 10,000 years in its formation identity. Expose them and optional actual age stages and include them in recipe/checkpoint identities. Do not regenerate for a camera-only change. The existing runner already supports Native/Headless/Rendered, seed/dimensions/cell size, point, resume, TerrainFlight, InspectTerrainFlight, WeatherFields, FloodFields and CloudView. Extend those capabilities without multiplying entry points, simulation implementations, test scenes or apps.
Provide stable documented command presets for formation/aging, terrain flight, water/flood, weather, terrain evolution, and integrated live flight. A preset is a reusable scenario in the same runner, not a separate solver or scene. Where relevant allow seed/size/age/step/stages or checkpoint, physical duration and pace, camera target in logical coordinates (X/Z plus optional elevation), distance, yaw/pitch, route/speed/hold settings, LOD count/maximum level and distances, optional display-only LOD inspection, resolution, fields and bounded capture/playback schedule. Use existing argument names where sensible; exact names/ranges are implementation details. Do not require irrelevant options for every preset. The normal rendered preset uses automatic LOD and physically advances; a fixed LOD, static observation or age playback is explicitly a diagnostic mode. Distinguish camera movement from physical time and geological age. Avoid full image history; reuse immutable sparse stages, stream or bound captures, and record actual source/recipe/time/geometry/binary identities. The main deliverable is reusable functionality, not new test infrastructure, cinematic editing or a polished UI. Provide one short runnable command example per completed area in the existing README and demonstrate it once with actual outputs. Let the user/Codex replay later with different settings.
Execution discipline and stopping
Two actual local Codex worker chats (not subagents) with longer implementation packages, controlled by a main GPT-6.2 Very High/Extra High orchestration chat where supported; see execution protocol. Workers should focus on delivering complete mechanisms and reusable presets, not report-only trials. Distinct worktrees/branches and isolated mutable caches/outputs; preserve immutable compatible inputs where safe. Serialize guarded heavy jobs on the shared PC, keep the one-writer rule and do not duplicate full builds just to parallelize. Main chat dispatches only ready independent work, ends its turn rather than polling, reviews returned receipts/diffs, integrates, and dispatches the next substantial package. Escalate real architecture decisions or blockers only. Batch documentation and public site updates by substantial package; canonical Brain remains authoritative and public mirror exact revision is verified. No repeated micro-publications or private GitHub Actions. No restart of completed work. No claim of implementation from this plan alone.

environmental-foundation-v1-execution.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — execution protocol
environmental-foundation-v1-execution.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — execution protocol
Authorized 26 November 2026. This operational protocol accompanies the full technical implementation plan and the progress record. It governs the user’s intended GPT-6.2 Very High/Extra High main local orchestration chat and two actual local implementation worker chats. Model naming and actual delegation capabilities depend on the available Codex interface; do not pretend to control another chat if the interface does not support it. No new engine code or test execution is claimed here.
Mission
Complete M0 preparation and every delivery milestone M1–M5 of the technical plan as one continuous full replacement. Deliver real integrated functionality, not a report-only pilot. The new implementation is the standard for fresh worlds; remove/disconnect superseded environmental mechanisms and legacy selection paths when the replacement is ready. Do not keep a second production water system, duplicate atmosphere, legacy compatibility layer, or old save conversion merely for continuity. Keep useful gameplay, Godot/Jolt, existing Zylann terrain integration, actual physical contracts, and historical evidence. Protect unrelated local changes, assets, user saves and installations.
Follow the current A–F package sequence in the active environment-only plan: fast reusable development baseline; terrain loading and continent-to-local rendering; water; weather; ongoing terrain evolution; integrated environmental evidence. These complete remaining M1–M5 rather than restart delivered work. All colony/actor/navigation/settlement work is out of scope, not merely population-scale qualification. Complete ecology, other liquids and unrelated legacy repair remain deferred.
Orchestrator and worker

Orchestrator: executes the user-approved end-to-end Brain plan, dependency manifest, sequence and integration boundaries; the user and planning chat retain fundamental architecture decisions. Read latest canonical Brain and actual worker receipts. Give the worker concrete bounded implementation packages with source pin, scope, acceptance, target paths if known, dependency order and commit/report expectations. Use independent implementation judgement, not micromanagement. Review exact diffs and evidence for changed paths, resolve routine issues, adjust reversible tunables, then immediately advance to next package/milestone. No request for approval simply because one package or milestone finishes.
Worker: owns actual code/build/edit work in the assigned checkout. Implement the selected existing algorithms and minimal native adapters; prefer reuse, simple data structures and physical consistency. Make necessary related call-site changes and remove superseded paths rather than preserve old environmental architecture. Perform only the directly useful checks, fix local issues within scope, record actual results and report the exact code commit, changed capabilities, incomplete requirements, checks, costs and any real blocker. Return work that runs where feasible, not pseudocode or fixture-only substitution. Do not invent a new solver or change fundamental architecture, requirement or scope without explicit user approval.
One writer per checkout. Orchestrator is accountable for canonical documentation and publication; worker supplies evidence and may author assigned docs when ownership is explicitly handed off. Coordinate via commits and the durable progress record, not duplicated work. Use actual local Codex chats, not subagents. Verify that the interface supports creating, messaging and receiving returned messages from those chats. If that mechanism is unavailable, report the limitation and provide two self-contained worker handoffs for the user to start/return; do not substitute subagents, invent a chat API or claim a message was sent. A separate chat does not automatically receive messages or keep running merely because another chat has been prompted.
Continue across all milestones within available execution sessions. If a context/session boundary occurs, save a precise continuation with the next executable package, current commit and real open issue; do not claim background execution or completion. Neither agent stops for routine design choices, optimization tradeoffs within the accepted architecture, ordinary builds/fixes or milestones. Do not create automated infinite loops or repeat failed attempts without changing the diagnosis.

Implementation-first verification
Minimum purposeful verification, not zero verification. Use the same small connected world and concise directly relevant checks for changed numerical/geometry behavior. Reuse upstream tests where useful, without reproducing all scientific benchmarks. Use the cheapest relevant execution mode of the one permanent environment baseline; native checks need no Godot launch. Launch the shared Godot scene for changed rendering/streaming or engine integration, not every package. Use quick targeted profiling and representative combined scale/visual checks at M5, with enough repeat/diagnostic detail to make measured claims meaningful. Run additional checks only to diagnose a consequential failure. Prefer fixing the feature over writing a large verification framework. Do not run exhaustive old regression suites, full legacy compatibility campaigns, performance matrices for every candidate, or repair unrelated failing tests. Keep Brain’s normal automated validation and safe publication; it is not a competing physics campaign.
Do not waive finite water/heat exchanges, sealed-barrier correctness, meaningful downstream consequences, current geometry, offscreen progression, persistence and actual weather. Preserve honest units/clocks and evidence. A playable approximation is appropriate; scientific forecast precision is not the goal. Do not label performance, scale or unexecuted functionality as passed. Historical targets and proposed acceptance tolerances remain as in the technical plan; choose meaningful local tolerances before checking, not after failure. If target hardware unavailable, say so and continue other implementable work; don’t block every feature on exhaustive target certification.
Stop and escalate only when necessary
Escalate if the primary upstream method is fundamentally unsuitable, a substantial bespoke numerical solver would be required, a hard physical requirement or performance envelope cannot be achieved without a product tradeoff, a material dependency/license change or fundamental clock/gameplay choice needs approval, or real permission/hardware/access/safety constraints make further meaningful work impossible. First make a bounded diagnosis and attempt the smallest compatible fix; do not spend days on circular tuning. Continue independent unblocked work where sensible. Report: exact failure or conflict, evidence, what has been tried, impact on the plan, one recommended path, and the precise decision or research question. Do not stop simply to ask for routine confirmation. Do not suppress the blocker to mark a milestone complete.
Two-repository workflow

Canonical private repo: github.com/caleb-var/godot_aokana. Inspect actual HEAD, nested AGENTS, local ownership and remote state. Create a reviewable implementation branch/worktree from appropriate runtime source head, synchronize the active V1 plan/authorization, commit coherent code changes and push for review. New runtime becomes the default fresh-world implementation on this branch; use normal repository merge controls rather than force-push or overwrite unrelated work.
Canonical authored documentation resides under docs/brain/content/ in the same private repo. The authorized publication ref is docs/breachborn-brain-refresh-20261125. Keep this ref current via a dedicated documentation worktree or controlled small docs-only commits based on its latest head. Reflect relevant records in the implementation branch as needed; do not merge unrelated runtime changes onto the docs branch. Avoid parallel writers and reconcile automatic generated-index commits before each update. Use stable IDs/typed edges, preserve existing records and historical negative evidence. Update affected systems, contracts, candidate selection/status, requirements traceability, and the V1 progress record after each meaningful package/milestone. Keep intent/selected/implemented/verified separate and cite exact source/code revision.
Public generated repo: github.com/caleb-var/breachborn-brain, main; live site caleb-var.github.io/breachborn-brain/. Never manually edit public generated files, copy private code/history/saves, or expose credentials or confidential local details. Author canonical Markdown, run python docs/brain/tools/atlas.py --write, python docs/brain/tools/atlas.py --check and python docs/brain/tools/test_brain.py when available, then commit/push the authorized docs ref. Use the cached local publication procedure in Brain workflow and docs/brain/tools/publish_local.py --publish. Do not spend private Actions minutes on ordinary edits. Confirm exact source and generated mirror revisions and deployed public source marker after meaningful publication; if publication fails or lags, use current canonical records and report the lag. Never bypass publication safety. Do not wait on routine asynchronous publication before implementing the next independent package. A failed mirror publication does not erase canonical progress.
Do not expose private source snippets, logs, filesystem details, or sensitive user data in publicly authored records. Keep detailed private runtime evidence outside docs/brain/content/ where necessary and publish safe summaries and reference identities.

Progress and completion
Provide concise progress receipts at integrated packages and every milestone, without waiting for a user reply: completed/working, exact commits, changes from plan, directly relevant checks and measured/estimated distinction, unresolved issue, documentation commit and mirror status, next work. Persist them in the progress record and relevant canonical system records. Use one lightweight status record, not a custom orchestration platform.
Final report: implemented M1–M5 capability status, actual default-path replacement, remaining known limitations, measured scale/CPU/GPU/RAM/debt and visual evidence where available, commits/PRs, dependency notices and canonical Brain publication state. Do not call an unfinished or unmeasured implementation complete. The user wants maximum implementation, not maximum paperwork.
27 November 2026 — controlling execution correction
One permanent, reusable environment-only development baseline for Codex, not a user-facing application. Native C++/headless execution is preferred for numerical work when cheaper; use the same underlying V1 owners and at most one active Godot environmental development scene for rendering, streaming and integration. UI is optional and not a deliverable. Reuse existing code and artifacts, never create a new scene or simulation for each test. No colonist creation, ticks, walking, scheduling, navigation/settlement work, benchmarking, optimization or compatibility work in this scope. Colonists will be revisited separately; preserve existing unrelated source and saves, not their current implementation as a requirement.
The user and planning chat own substantive architecture decisions through the canonical Brain. Codex follows the selected stack, requirements and contracts; it may make bounded implementation fixes, dependency-aware build changes, safe caches and reversible configuration choices within that design. Do not reopen solver/renderer selection, replace Zylann, change authoritative ownership, physical clocks, requirements, major dependencies, or scope without explicit user approval. Report an evidenced fundamental blocker and a concrete recommendation; continue independent in-scope work.
Follow active delivery packages A–F. Make development fast first; then fast terrain loading and exceptionally smooth real 3D continent-to-ground zoom; then finish water, weather, evolution and combined qualification. Reuse one suitable primary world and compatible build/checkpoint artifacts. Larger-scale runs only for actual scale/coverage questions, not mandatory repeated matrices. Use minimal directly relevant checks and batched real field outputs. Do not create another showcase, debug UI, competing scene or solver. Existing tests and historic receipts remain evidence, not recurring gates. Keep 8x environment-only reference goal and 60 FPS reference goal; 32x and all colony work deferred. This controls over any conflicting earlier instructions.
Two local implementation chats — 27 November 2026
Caleb authorized two local GPT-6.2 Sol chats for the remaining environment work. One chat writes and owns the single guarded workload while the other reviews a frozen commit and prepares the next coherent implementation streak. Transfer writing and job ownership explicitly when useful. Review actual effects, relevant source and retained measurements at substantial checkpoints. Group dependent implementation and use the smallest observation that answers the changed physical or performance question. Continue independent work during review. The canonical plan and its architecture decision authority still control.
Brain publication correction — 27 November 2026
Routine Brain updates must not trigger private GitHub Actions. Build and validate locally with cached Quartz dependencies, then publish only generated output using the local publisher. Batch ordinary evidence at meaningful implementation checkpoints; publish accepted requirement/architecture changes promptly. Confirm exact canonical and mirror source revisions and actual public deployment; if stale, use the canonical branch and report the lag. Do not use private Actions as a routine fallback or manually edit generated public files.
27 November 2026 — fresh two-worker completion campaign (controlling)
Read the remaining packages and reusable demonstration contract in the active plan. The main local chat uses GPT-6.2 with Very High (Extra High where that is the label) thinking, and controls exactly two actual local worker chats where the interface supports it. Worker 1 owns formation/aging, standard terrain streaming/LOD and environment presentation. Worker 2 owns finite water, physical weather and natural terrain evolution. Give each a substantial ready package with exact starting commit, explicit owned paths/shared-interface responsibilities, acceptance and reusable command example. Let workers run long independent implementation turns. No routine check-ins, repetitive status questions or micro-task delegation. They report on completion or a consequential blocker: pushed commit, actual implementation, direct checks and measurements, reusable commands, remaining limitations, any conflicting changes.
Main chat is the integration/review/plan owner, not another parallel writer. Stop/hand off the prior writer safely; inspect dirty/untracked changes before assigning separate worktrees/branches. Coordinate shared preview/session/binding/runner files and merge only after review. Single writer per checkout and mutable cache, protected saved artifacts, serialize heavy guarded jobs; no parallel Godot/build contention on the shared PC. When a worker returns, read its receipt and relevant diff, resolve bounded integration defects or send a focused corrective handoff, then dispatch the next ready package. Do not make the other worker redo a completed check. Use practical context and token economy; no continuous polling/wait loop. After dispatching, end the main chat turn; resume only on actual returned worker message or user request. Do not promise autonomous communication unsupported by the local interface.
Send concise progress or a material decision/review request to the user’s Dot only if an authorized working channel is available; otherwise leave the summary and next action in the main chat. No frequent notifications, no invented message delivery. Publish canonical Brain and generated site together at meaningful completed packages and accepted requirement changes, not every micro-fix. No private Actions minutes. Preserve physical invariants, full V1 scope and no-colonist lock. Reusable tests are required deliverables, but no separate test product or repetitive visual campaign. If blocked on an architectural change, report evidence and recommendation, continue independent work, and ask the user for that decision only. Finish F and stop; do not turn V1 into indefinite optimization.

environmental-foundation-v1-progress.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation progress
environmental-foundation-v1-progress.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation progress
Updated 27 November 2026. Technical plan and execution protocol govern this full replacement.








































MilestoneStatusEvidenceM0 Prepare and pinReusable baseline verifiedOne guarded native, headless and Forward+ runner reuses compatible builds, immutable recipes and physical checkpoints.M1 Aged editable terrainGeometry and streaming verified within measured workloadsVersioned relief, current voxels, refined coastal support and a live 15-LOD 4,000 km flight. The opt-in native clipbox budget removed the measured macro frame spike in its replay. Installed integration and final presentation quality remain open.M2 Water replacementIn progressConnected rivers, lake spills, ocean, CFE catchments, groundwater, a measured cave outlet, regional floods and recession. The surveyed fine parcel qualified for automatic admission, calm return and cold continuation. A current marine floor edit repaired an existing basin and reopened with its measured depth. Wider concurrent automatic coverage, restriction after a new rapid edit, arbitrary lateral cave outlets and general shoreline topology changes remain open. Same-owner dry-to-wet, deepening, full solid-fill return and cross-atmosphere-cell area conservation are verified within bounded cases.M3 Live coupled weatherIn progressEight-layer mixed-phase transport, conservative finite surface exchange and optical-distance rendering of accepted condensate. Connected storms, cold recovery and a fixed-view overcast comparison have been measured. Distinct cloud silhouettes remain open.M4 Erosion and visual worldIn progressSediment-accounted edits move current survey frames and incrementally change the hydraulic arc and subsequent bend weights. Cold restoration recovered the same geometry. A supported natural cutoff and wider migrating river footprints remain open.M5 Integrated scaleIn progressThe 100 km reference storm sustained 8.200× and 60.01 FPS. An inundated 100 km continuation with a moving camera and current floor edit reached 8.044× through save and 60.05 FPS. The 4,000 km storm with a local camera reached 8.169× and 60.05 FPS. The advancing opt-in 15-LOD continuation with asynchronous captures reached 8.183× through save and 59.964 FPS. Whole-route 60 FPS, wider active-flood workloads and final presentation remain open.
Current continuation — user decision, 27 November 2026
Execute packages A–F now: one reusable Codex-only development baseline (no UI required), dependency-aware incremental builds, compatible cached recipes/checkpoints; then resolve terrain streaming and smooth continent-to-local 3D LOD; complete water, weather, erosion/migration and representative integrated environment-only qualification. No colony/actor/navigation/settlement integration, tests or compatibility work. Prior colony receipts below remain historical evidence; they are not current acceptance workloads. Runtime inspected at a891cc78. Keep all previous evidence, actual open physical issues and reference performance goals.
Current completion handoff — 27 November 2026
Planning reviewed runtime 75b7520a and Brain 97c45754. A is verified. User requests finishing all V1 capabilities with a reusable, configurable command-driven scenario for each system, actual aging playback, faster and higher-quality full-continent LOD/streaming, moving clouds and corresponding actual weather fields. Use the controlling remaining packages and test contract and two-local-worker execution protocol. Main work remains standard clipbox integration and terrain quality, generalized water and adaptive concurrent fine flow, weather/presentation closure (including moving-cloud failure), natural cutoff/migration and final integration. No colony work. This is authorized continuation, not new code or test evidence.
Package A — reusable environment development baseline
Implementation 6be158c7 adds one guarded command with native, headless Godot and Forward+ modes. Both physical paths use the existing V1 terrain recipe and the same native water/weather initialization. The runner maintains one Godot staging project, reuses pinned compiler products using actual MSVC include dependencies, and keys immutable recipes separately from physical checkpoints. Run outputs use isolated scratch directories. No colony or navigation resources are staged.
The first guarded build took 70.9 s. Warm preparation took 4.15–4.44 s and reused all 20 native products. A native diagnostic edit rebuilt only its translation unit and executable. Changing the formation from 64 × 48 km to 65 × 48 km generated a distinct recipe and the requested storm checkpoint without recompiling. The seed-713 64 × 48 km recipe is the default. Its native and headless Godot 20 s continuations matched byte-for-byte, with checkpoint SHA-256 7ff39bc874c331549db9a04889022693782ccef71005bf614285956c89722e4e. An independent Forward+ process resumed the native result through 30 s and captured the current local terrain at X 15,500 m, Z 17,500 m. It copied no unchanged project resources. The tested binding SHA-256 is d15bcc8776c6d47628a8701745369d05a7c13b6d30de78160dd07f3071cd269b. The corrected native executable SHA-256 is d80e08a33b9790f7dc57b71b853ed6c7cf1fcb4b87dbb4b2aac5b0bab405e306. Scope is development reuse and shared continuation. Package B now measures and improves actual streaming and continent-to-local 3D detail.
Package B — Zylann terrain streaming and editable LODs
Implementation 487dc399 keeps one Zylann/Transvoxel terrain from overview through the editable metre lattice. Zylann sizes the coarsest clipbox level to the generated extent and uses bounded finer shells. Complementary fades smooth the mesh switch. Bounded V1 worlds use floating-point SDF so distant cells can interpolate physical distances through the existing mesher. Current reads, edits, saved parent blocks and the generator identity use that format. Worker-local X/Z column reuse and constant material weights reduce redundant generation work. The terrain flight rebases nearby rendering using the existing RegionWorld origin while retaining logical coordinates.
