The pre-change 64 × 48 km flight showed blank overview and regional frames. The adjusted 64 × 48 km flight reached all nine overview probes and an edit with matching saved parent data. The final 512 × 512 km Forward+ flight used the cached 4 km recipe and twelve Zylann levels. Warm first visible terrain was 0.521 s and all nine overview probes were covered by 0.682 s. The local current read became usable 6.55 ms after the local lease was requested, at 7.27 s into the timed approach. A terrain edit at (182000, 604, 10000) changed the local SDF from −1.880249 m to +0.1875 m, with the same +0.1875 m in the persisted four-metre parent sample. It flushed eight verified LOD0 blocks. Peak counts were 33,726 data blocks and 603 mesh blocks. Warm kernel job peak was 800 MiB, with frame p95 11.82 ms, render CPU p95 0.37 ms and render GPU p95 1.48 ms. Binding SHA-256 4592b9b8e28156fb1dcbefc00b9f1ae8defaa376e42beaceb73abe62ebf4ddea. Startup, overview, regional and near captures and the readiness timeline are retained with the guarded receipts.
A shader-cold run took 1.51 s to first visible terrain and included a 1.08 s startup frame. The warm flight still had a 101 ms worst frame. Integrated weather, finished water and terrain presentation, and 4,000 km rendered scale remain later qualification. Package C continues the connected water implementation on the reusable environment baseline.
Package C checkpoint — current regional water geometry
Implementation 8db29d7d measures water-affected edits through bounded camera-independent current voxel leases and publishes repaired feature groups independently. Untouched regions can advance while affected geometry is held. Reports identify a held survey and its required bounds. Channel strips share an atomic coarse owner. The measured flood bed remains held when a valid crossing is unavailable. The current cave survey accepts floating-point voxel distance. Water and terrain publish as a paired checkpoint with the current terrain revision.
In the ordinary 64 × 48 km environment, three edits affected two wet reaches more than 10 km apart and a separate cave. Terrain invalidation left current surface inventory unchanged. The coupled owners accepted 10 s while geometry was held and completed seven surveys. The measured beds fell 1.879 m and 2.203 m, and the surveyed cave capacity was 5,304 m³. Four current blocks and water at 30 s were saved at terrain revision 3. A fresh Godot process verified the saved water bytes, read the edited terrain and advanced to 40 s at that same revision. The loaded extension SHA-256 is 2515b1836d26afe0ad9416aeae6948c574f63ca6001ee73a96b5a2f868fd232a. This checkpoint also restores the pending sparse flow optimization. Regional flood rise and recession, remaining cave outlets and expanded rapid ownership are still open in Package C.
Package C checkpoint — finite regional flooding and recession
Implementation 14e0805e adds a bounded native hydrograph through the shared environment baseline. The seed-713 64 × 48 km storm advanced from 0 to 5,400 s and independently reopened through 21,600 s. Floodplain storage rose from zero to 237,150 m³ at 9,600 s, then receded by 5,239 m³. Up to 1,041 flood compartments contained water. At 21,600 s the network showed 1,743 flowing faces, two flowing basin spills, 6.31 million m³ of accepted runoff and 6.95 m³ of cumulative spring discharge. A coastal face flowed during the continuation. Up to 137 faces used the rapid regime, and the first process recorded one accepted FluxCell fine-pair return.
The largest observed combined water and net-radiation-adjusted heat residuals over the two process intervals were 0.065 m³ and 99.4 MJ, relative to starting stocks of 1.374 trillion m³ and 1.646 × 10²¹ J. The 21,600 s native accepted intervals took 85.39 s including diagnostic sampling. Native executable SHA-256 8874ca36ca2ceb48a510f5131e1749dd813ca9703d2ed9c999a8bcbae965f0e4. The rainfall tail continued during recession, and retained water remained in the represented floodplains. This establishes regional rise and recession in the primary development world. Large-world rendered throughput and general current-geometry rapid and cave qualification remain open.
Package C checkpoint — live presentation, rapid water and cave discharge
Implementation 3f0ced8a uses the shared water renderer in the environment-only host. It reads accepted river, lake, coastal and flood stores and responds to current hydraulic publications. A Forward+ run continued the native storm from 5,400 to 5,410 s and captured the cut channel and accepted water geometry. The local submission included one reach, three flood cells, one lake and one marine body.
Implementation 0c4ca110 applies the selected FluxCell kernel to measured flood geometry with concurrent incident faces. An exclusive pair can return both finite parcels. With concurrent faces the fine solve proposes volume and the regional owner admits all debits simultaneously with heat and tracers in the same commit. The unedited 5,400 s checkpoint remained byte-identical. A headless wet continuation updated ten surveys and produced 21 coupled measured proposals through 5,700 s. A fresh process restored revision 4 and made another 11 through 6,000 s. Combined residuals for the latter interval were 0.0039 m³ and 2.51 MJ at full-stock scale. The loaded binding SHA-256 was f8cf19fd5600b13adb3c6edb8f4f670cc265fbf4858e43e44e29dd0a36099bbb.
Implementation 4d82564c includes the surveyed vertical shaft in cave capacity and admits groundwater discharge through its open mouth. Available head, aperture and receiving capacity bound the exchange. The native 128 km probe used a finite metered supply and surveyed four square metres of opening. It filled the remaining 0.75 m³ at the crest and discharged 2.25 m³ of mixed water with heat and both tracers when the driving head was sufficient. The independently reconstructed owner reproduced the checkpoint bytes. This is a controlled head probe over generated geometry. Arbitrary lateral cave cuts, persistent whole-parcel fine ownership in the regional network and world-scale water presentation remain open. Package D continues on the same coupled baseline.
The 128 km scene now also verifies the opposite direction through a real Zylann excavation. An existing sealed chamber opened after terrain revision 1. The current voxel survey found a 1 m² aperture at the 1,920 m crest and reproduced 5,404 m³ of supported chamber capacity. Existing river head supplied 14.95636 m³ after 10 s, with 17.89711 GJ, 7.95 × 10⁻⁵ kg of solute and 1.19 × 10⁻⁴ kg of suspended sediment from a finite tracer dose. A cold process restored the paired terrain and continued to 20 s with 29.83789 m³, 35.70468 GJ and 1.48448 m³/s of river intake at the saved boundary. The initial and cold checkpoint SHA-256 values were a56964dcc8631009cc6f48cf28fe65b922eb4a1acfaf5cf0bdfca0eca56a1303 and 4bbc275f1e98848c9644ddbe002046f130fa06f857432f94949cf557084ad242. The measured binding is f775c0e8fe0d60a6173e211277cf773bccdedb27aaa3199d85c43c4ca5ddb673. This case supports a real vertical river contact and cold continuation. Lateral outlets still need matching current geometry and a verified finite connection. Implementation 15924908
A bounded lateral candidate separated the surveyed exterior face, the connected throat and the passage air volume under the existing river and cave IDs. In the cached 128 km world, the only eligible wet river contact had 1,920.62709 m of cover level against the 1,921.5 m required by the measured two-metre approach. No cut was attempted there. The retained 100 km storm had a covered site at chamber 1688849860273214. Its real riser stayed sealed for an accepted ten-second interval. A subsequent 7 × 2 × 2 m adjoining excavation at (27000, 338, 42500) exposed a face outside the supported river mouth. Measuring fractional open height still identified that unsupported contact. The link stayed closed with zero river intake and the chamber kept 1.360715 m³. The lateral candidate and its receipts are retained outside the release branch. Fixed topology still needs an exterior face inside the existing river support or a separately authorized connection to another physical recipient.
Implementation e8cdc6ff requests current sill surveys for every open port when an edit enrolls a detailed flood compartment. At 5,400 s in the 64 × 48 km storm, compartment 281474977253128 had 0.000129 m³/s entering through one port and 0.001002 m³/s leaving through another. The headless current-voxel repair measured its 144 floor points and nine sill points on each of three open ports. The rest of the environment accepted 10 s while surveys were held. The compartment retained 47.813856 m³ through repair. The 5,420 s checkpoint SHA-256 is e1fe70e23cddb84b32b6aa7b7cc9d11a0b835ad39f85db4ac7053723b2d608da and the binding SHA-256 is 3a074629ec838b0b496fce31870a446d3741f1ba318635143adb9e28d6e0e716. The footprint is ready for a bounded persistent fine parcel trial. Fine momentum and finite port receipts across intervals remain unverified. The prior edited return refusal stands.
Implementation b389bf5b retains the metre-scale FluxCell distribution and velocities of the surveyed 12 m flood compartment across accepted surface intervals. The existing store is the single inventory. FluxCell supplies closed-interior substeps and sill-limited port proposals. The regional owner admits finite transfers in its simultaneous budget, and each accepted port moves water, enthalpy, solute and suspended sediment together. One explicit development admission uses the same edited terrain and the advancing coupled Godot session. The fine calculation is bounded to one warm parcel and uses first-order exterior port states. The third measured port remained hydraulically inactive in the observed interval.
The 5,420–5,440 s headless trial added 0.02 m³ of 279 K water with 2 g solute and 3 g suspended sediment. Two ports conveyed nonzero quantities of all four lanes in both directions over the measured interval. Total port inflow was 3.3103 m³ and outflow 13.7912 m³. Maximum local residuals were 4.27 × 10⁻¹⁴ m³, 4.58 × 10⁻⁵ J, 8.68 × 10⁻¹⁹ kg solute and 2.17 × 10⁻¹⁸ kg suspended sediment. The full environment interval had −0.00269 m³ water and −1.02 MJ net heat residual against about 1.37 × 10¹² m³ and 1.65 × 10²¹ J. A cold process restored 0.19139 m/s peak fine velocity at 5,430 s and advanced the next 10 s. It reached the same 5,440 s checkpoint as the uninterrupted host, SHA-256 224dc14d5b1cd04ee1fde7aab8903d1c6ca0a0711bbd77e3a6e3d171384bef3a. The final verified cold binding SHA-256 is b41e689fcc2075c33d93d8ce53355be9a989ccc1623ecb899953d36117b37375. The active windows took 207.59 ms for 20 s direct and 113.32 ms for 10 s after cold open. They are small headless trials. Automatic persistent admission, substantial mixed-phase fine transport and restriction after edits remain unqualified.
Implementation 9ebe3334 admits one persistent patch at the existing ten-second detail epoch. It ranks already measured liquid compartments with complete bed and port support, at least two wet exchanges and an existing rapid face or slope outside the ordinary-flow regime. It uses accepted discharge and sill-limited head to rank candidates. Pending bed or port geometry holds the affected exchanges and retains the fine state. Other regional flows remain eligible.
The unmetered 64 × 48 km storm resumed at 5,420 s with no fine parcel. In the normal headless path, compartment 281474977253127 was selected automatically and remained active for the full 20 s. Three ports took in a combined 10.81225 m³ and one of those ports also released 4.42927 m³ over the interval. Maximum local volume and heat residuals were 3.56 × 10⁻¹⁴ m³ and 4.58 × 10⁻⁵ J. A separate process restored the 0.37554 m/s peak fine velocity at 5,430 s and reproduced the uninterrupted 5,440 s result, including the 0.60536 m/s ending peak and checkpoint SHA-256 8ef0a304c3e82d1d3e0730c6c087b27e9156a0687eb8a512364a06bc85df3b10. Binding SHA-256 a6b5201c49ff018f03f1c3c4547f68ff8f508f1bd4aff993c40157cfec6f69f6. The direct 20 s headless advance took 267.68 ms. The 10 s cold continuation took 172.72 ms. These times cover the coupled advance and do not isolate patch cost or establish scaled throughput. The natural case carried water and heat. The earlier metered case establishes the two tracer lanes. Mixed-phase fine flow, multiple concurrent patches and edited restriction remain open.
The environmental point query now reports retained fine depths and world-space velocity using the current surveyed footprint. At 5,440 s, all 144 metre-square points were wet. Query depths integrated to 61.4513561410018 m³ against 61.4513561410019 m³ in the owner. Peak sample depth was 2.49440 m and peak speed was 0.60536 m/s. The cold query retained the exact checkpoint and used binding SHA-256 c0e6883ca45e57231d8b9a4f3ff9bb502ee49500590be26c82c28f483b548ecf. Implementation 18294c33
The shared Forward+ water view draws the same 144 wet cells as one mesh against current Zylann terrain. It averages wet-neighbour heights at shared corners and projects the accepted depth-weighted flow into the existing water material. The cold capture retained revision 4 and the exact 5,440 s checkpoint. It submitted 326 water triangles overall, including 288 from the fine compartment. The local capture establishes the physical wet shape and still shows abrupt boundaries at surrounding coarse contacts. A first renderer load failure was corrected. The preview now reports failure if it cannot instantiate water presentation. Implementation 0417d08c
One current Zylann excavation lowered an interior fine floor from 232.06425 to 229.50000 m in the automatically admitted compartment. From 5,440 to 5,450 s the patch held all port receipts and its 61.47136 m³, 70.35724 GJ, 2 g solute and 3 g suspended sediment while the surrounding environment advanced. The same 144 floor points and existing port surveys supported resumed fine exchange through 5,460 s. The largest observed local residuals across the retained receipts were 3.56 × 10⁻¹⁴ m³ and 4.58 × 10⁻⁵ J. Implementation 9bbc8f5d
The new restriction gate keeps the same store and port momentum. It requires current support, matching aggregate capacity, one connected coarse pool and a downhill route from the fine sheet to that pool. It requires fine motion below the existing rapid-flow release threshold. The edited case still reached Froude 1.769 over materially wet cells, so restriction was refused after the repair. An independent process restored revision 5 and accepted another 10 s with the fine parcel retained. It held 29.57668 m³ at 5,470 s and peak Froude remained 1.830. The 5,460 and 5,470 s checkpoint SHA-256 values were ccd7cbb53aa6971dfa430cdad1878b61e12ffae270d331158542350b676e515d and 84c65344fc276fcaa33f844804d8aed0fcf0cd48fcb411dda7a770b35cfcd86b. The binding SHA-256 was f775c0e8fe0d60a6173e211277cf773bccdedb27aaa3199d85c43c4ca5ddb673. Safe edited hold and continued fine custody are qualified. A successful edited restriction and the earlier wider unsupported return remain open.
Implementation 563ec9d8 automatically checks the same restriction gate at the existing 10 s detail boundary after at least 20 s of fine activity and with all port Froude values below the release threshold. In the same 64 × 48 km storm, the measured calmer compartment 281474977253128 could restrict to its existing coarse store at 5,440 s. Its 144 current floor points, three links and parcel were unchanged at the transaction. Stock was 62.01093 m³, 70.94939 GJ, 1.63745 g solute and 2.44879 g suspended sediment. The largest accepted port Froude was 0.002345. The exact same-time coarse checkpoint was 8c43cfa3cbfc1afa552dbf26111fa5b11af74e158bd2dbee796733ecccf5b8a4.
The normal path then consumed the original fine checkpoint without a manual restrict command. By 5,470 s the one fine slot had moved to neighbouring compartment 281474977253127. The 30 s advance took 260.26 ms and had +0.00391 m³ water, +4.316 MJ heat and 4.34 × 10⁻¹⁹ kg sediment residuals. A cold process verified that paired state, restored the neighbour and accepted another 10 s. At 5,480 s the slot was clear. The 5,470 and 5,480 s checkpoints are 80fd2c2962821ea8419a9dfa60d8bc1d0bf77a26f7f95b1216607a6777a824c0 and f5e6a9da0cb9ca04604ac38729db10340177bd92784fa0d77a786dd82a857256. Both loaded binding aed2d804431ad67319f8428872d6c9a3bd9fe7d78d6b27207ed0fe2ff1c4d070. This verifies bounded return on existing surveyed terrain and re-use of one slot. The separate high-Froude excavation and unsupported wider geometry remain outside the return witness.
Package C follow-up — renewed rapid flow after coarse return
Implementation 6b6830fc remembers a calm fine-to-coarse return on the existing surveyed compartment. The subdivision can admit again after a quiescent interval, a measured critical port, or revised current geometry. Persisting the return gate prevents a cold process from reading a fixed steep grade as a new event. The coarse face, stock, heat, constituent and terrain ownership paths are unchanged.
The 64 × 48 km rendered storm started at 5,440 s with the naturally admitted patch already 20 s old. The initial 200 s observation ran at 7.95242× viewport pace and 60.04 FPS. It ended with a 10 s-old patch at the same compartment, establishing at least one return and re-admission. The matched physical-gate run recorded two restrictions, one later admission and zero remaining fine patches at 5,640 s. Starting presentation drew 144 fine cells. The viewport ran at 7.96824× and 60.04 FPS, with p95/p99/max frame times of 16.694/16.828/17.011 ms and at most one complete weather quantum of debt. Full advance wrappers were 25.6329 s (7.80247×) and 25.8567 s (7.73493×). Both scenes included volumetric clouds and one sediment-accounted terrain edit. These short windows demonstrate the transition behavior and give no isolated patch cost or strict 8× qualification.
The corrected 5,640 s payload d0d198b53a01951e20c34bfad0e7add5c63dc45f775f999ffa4591fad4972be7 independently continued to 5,660 s with no new fine admissions or restrictions. The same terrain bytes were retained. Coupled water and heat residuals over that continuation were −0.00928 m³ and +6.838 MJ. The continued payload is ad78539ffc9c2d29b92fa0fcab03276009733fd69dcda65fda91dd2633517688 and the loaded binding is 92e9b338c3370c5a214df1dc8438b1440b4a6856ccd53e62c2f839a26a5b25e8. Evidence persistent-flood-paced-5640, persistent-flood-paced-rearm-5640 and persistent-flood-rearm-cold-5660. Sustained cost of continuously rapid finer work and wider simultaneous active patches remain open.
Package C follow-up — liquid FluxCell flow in a mixed-phase compartment
Implementation 78625821 lets the measured fine compartment transport its mobile liquid while its existing owner retains the bulk ice and associated enthalpy. Surveyed depths receive the ice water-equivalent displacement. The mobile liquid uses its bulk equilibrium enthalpy when ice is present, with independent solute and sediment shares. 128568ed gives each supported generated spill a current-voxel survey at its controlling saddle. In a fresh normal 128 km colony a metered lake head produced flow through the existing outlet. A real stone terrain edit raised the measured crest by 2.790 m and stopped that connection while 141 others moved. A separate process restored the same measured barrier and advanced to 80 physical seconds. Current lake spill evidence
Background water and weather remove a frame-time bottleneck
a8c8f144 gives one native worker exclusive ownership of a bounded water and weather interval while the scene renders the last accepted state. The two scheduling paths produced identical checkpoint bytes from the same late 512 km storm. The normal 128-actor 512 km workload reached 300 physical seconds at 4.00× with 11.153 ms frame p95 and 14.854 ms p99. It independently reopened to 370 seconds. The measured early-storm frame times meet the 60 FPS threshold, and the 8× simulated throughput target remains open. Background cohort timing and custody
Retained floodwater infiltrates the connected catchment soil
dc533d3e uses the current surveyed bed and the existing CFE soil properties to move finite water from each wetted flood footprint into its underlying catchment. In ten seconds of the retained 512 km storm, 293 catchments received 20.533 m³ and 23.476 GJ. An independent native continuation reproduced the next checkpoint. The full recession response remains under measurement. Floodplain-to-soil evidence
Wet flood custody and accelerated actor publication
7f1a06a2 limits catchment infiltration to currently wet, supported compartments. The same 512 km storm checkpoint reproduced the exact next accepted state in both scheduling paths at 14,405 physical seconds. By 14,400 seconds the preceding storm continuation had delivered 5,003.384 m³ into catchment soil. The two observed regions retained 100,852 and 225,760 m³ with continuing inflows and return flows. Wet compartment and storm evidence
72a37daf batches accelerated actor ticks within a bounded publication gap. The rendered 512 km run reached 380 physical seconds in 75.373 wall seconds at 5.04×. It completed 96 walks with 128 actors present, recorded frame p95/p99 of 11.386/15.905 ms and independently reopened through 480 seconds. The early-storm run accumulated 219.782 s of queued actor work and hit a renderer instance-parameter allocation limit. Sustained 8× with full scene rendering remains open. Rendered actor workload and limitations
Current river contacts with lakes and the coast
0107ad7c gives the existing terminal channels their own repairable hydraulic sections. In the normal 512 km colony, two current stone berms stopped a 58.48 m³/s coastal outflow and a 22.50 m³/s backflow from a lake. Both connected stores at each contact retained the same water and heat at repair. Another 1,723 links kept flowing. A separate host reopened the paired save and verified the same barriers. Terminal repair evidence
Rendered 512 km colony keeps pace near 8×
9ee6b655 keeps small, mostly stationary crowds on the same numeric discovery path without a cross-frame worker wait and sizes the Forward+ buffer for streamed foliage fades. A normal 512 km run reached 1,160 physical seconds in 145.389 wall seconds at 7.98×. It finished with 0.88 ms of queued actor time, recorded 288 walks and six natural erosion events, and published moving volumetric clouds. Frame p95 was 15.021 ms and p99 was 20.770 ms. An independent normal process reopened the paired save and reached 1,170 seconds. The later fully inundated stage remains unmeasured in this rendered workload. Pacing, rendering and storm evidence
Naturally eroded sediment reaches previously unsurveyed channels
f115654d lets supported receiving reaches settle and remobilize suspended sediment before a terrain survey exists. Starting from the rendered 1,160-second storm save with six natural bed edits, another 120 seconds placed 819.640 kg in unplaced channel-bed stock across ten ordinary reaches. Independent continuation reproduced the accepted 1,300-second checkpoint. The material remains available for current bed placement when local conditions and the permitted terrain budget support an edit. Regional sediment custody
The rendered colony advances into regional inundation
The normal colony reopened the paired 1,160-second save with 128 actors and continued to 3,090 seconds with the regional sediment build. It completed 445 walks and ten additional current-voxel erosion events. Floodwater grew from 2,688 to 158,139 m³ across 1,162 wet compartments. The run averaged 7.85× with frame p95 of 15.224 ms. It ended with 28.597 seconds of actor work queued and reproduced a foliage shader allocation limit after the view streamed other terrain. A separate normal process reopened sequence 4 and advanced to 3,130 seconds. Rendered inundation and remaining gates
Local terrain repair and streamed foliage in the active flood
c046c744 indexes current flood and terminal surveys by physical location. Four disjoint notifications on the accepted 512 km storm selected seven survey sets and 614 samples. The prior and indexed builds wrote the same held and repaired state, including a cold restore while the surveys were held. Local terrain repair evidence
84b199d6 keeps the existing foliage distance fade and removes the per-batch uniform used for streaming fades. The rendered continuation reached 3,990 physical seconds with 248,612 m³ of floodwater and emitted zero renderer errors. It averaged 7.20× and ended with 122.729 s of queued actor work. The full active storm still misses the sustained 8× gate. Clean rendered active flood evidence
Snow reaches the finite wet surface directly
722b876a routes snow to the same mapped wet receiving areas as rain. It preserves the snow enthalpy until the receiving water takes custody. In the 512 km continuation from 3,990 to 4,090 seconds, 7,536.782 m³ water-equivalent reached wet surfaces and 5.446 m³ remained queued. An independent process restored both stocks and matched the continuing accepted state at 4,110 seconds. Solid precipitation and cold custody evidence
The normal colony reopens the rendered 4,000 km macro world
3b8bf140 exposes the macro workload through the normal colony host. The two weather regions sit about 2,485 km apart. The world used 35,907 catchments and 19,039 flood corridors, with 15,140 connections flowing in the fresh 260-second save. The corrected cold reopen crossed the first land exchange, saved at 360 seconds, and reopened independently at 420 seconds. The 4,000 km run demonstrated connected macro coverage and persistence, and is below the 8× production target. Normal macro evidence
bc681380 retains one exclusive weather worker and publishes complete colony quanta. In the active 512 km storm, synchronous and background paths wrote identical checkpoint bytes at 4,100 and 4,110 seconds. Resident worker evidence

environmental-foundation-v1-review-20261.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — independent continuation review
environmental-foundation-v1-review-20261.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — independent continuation review
26 November 2026. Review of implementation snapshot d1f1483b, canonical evidence 367d3ad, and the user’s reported Codex checkpoint. The public generated mirror was verified at 91ce97f02d8870a67d7ea5155dbf68ca54c7c547 (publication message for 367d3adfd101). This review inspected actual repository source and existing evidence; no independent runtime, hardware benchmark or image/capture inspection was performed. This is a recommended continuation of the authorized full replacement, not a new technology or requirement lock.
Historical source snapshot: This review remains evidence of the earlier implementation, not the active execution sequence. Later commits supersede some coverage findings; see progress. The current environment-only plan excludes all colonist/actor/navigation workloads and prioritizes reusable development and continuous terrain LOD.
Assessment
M1 core aged editable terrain and fresh-world admission are implemented in bounded cases. M2 and M3 have working upstream-derived physical kernels and a shared accepted clock, but normal-world coverage is still pilot-limited. M4 has real clouds and bounded flow-driven cuts, not general deposition or lateral migration/cutoffs. M5 has 64/128/256/512km save/reopens and 4,000km macro opening with two water neighborhoods (no regional weather or actors), not a representative full environment load. The latest 512km rendered day achieved 600s in 75.043s, zero ending debt, p95/p99 16.157/24.747ms; 32x reopen p95/p99 20.215/24.986ms, missed frame target. Sixteen actors, 25 atmosphere columns and one open pair. Preserve the user-confirmed 1:1 physical clock; 8x baseline, 32x stretch. Do not chase stretch performance before regional functionality.
Source-confirmed coverage bottleneck

Normal initialization fills marine stocks then selects the first eligible nonmarine connection and returns after initializing its coupled weather. Surface preparation creates a broader finite graph but ordinary links begin closed; formation basin capacity is not itself water. Natural connected links must operate in the normal world, not just one commanded demonstration. Initialize plausible finite stock and catchment feeding/spin-up; preserve closed controls and unresolved contacts.
LandWater has exactly two columns and two aquifers. Weather construction crops around those two receivers, uses terrain sample spacing, caps columns at 4096, and maps only those land/reach footprints. The warm regional 100x100km evidence used 2km² connected land (0.02% of domain area); approximately 354,410m³ of rain outside footprints stayed in weather ground stock, whereas about 1,677.57m³ entered CFE and 4.54m³ entered reaches directly. Rain exchange retains uncovered ground water and explicitly never reoffers it. This is finite accounting, not whole-area runoff. Generalize to all represented physical surfaces with conservative coarse catchments, no need for per-metre land owners. Route existing pending/retained stocks coherently; don’t silently discard rain. CFE interface has fixed 1,800 physical-second interval (three default 600s game days at 1:1); assess meaningful storm response and donor-consistent configurable cadence, not arbitrary coefficient/timestep changes.
Surface solver scans all stores/links per substep and returns before accepting high-Froude flow. Surface owner supports one 3x3 floodplain and singleton watched/delegated state. Regional wetting and rapid transfer must use independent connected storage, sparse actual work and bounded local detail. A steep coast or rapid patch must not permanently stop unrelated simulation; preserve finite custody and coherent time. Prior edited fine return lacks coarse survey coverage. Reuse proven kernels; generalize owning records and boundaries, don’t multiply copies of isolated pilots or create a second production engine.
Normal repair refuses survey counts other than one. Normal water view creates two bounded 240m strips, with 512m visibility distance, and hides on nonzero world revision. Generalize current-geometry repair and meaningful depth/velocity/hazard queries, show actual visible rivers, lakes, coast/flood water from current geometry, and update dirty portions rather than globally hiding. Normal gameplay edits and hazards are not yet accepted. No full navigation or ECS rewrite in V1.
Cold exchange applies current warm liquid exchange only with both air and water >=273.15K. Mixed regional receivers had air about 262–266K and zero CFE potential ET; snow/rain/melt still functioned. Zero potential ET in cold saturated conditions is not itself invalid. Do not force positive ET or choose an easier test to hide missing behavior. Implement physically eligible cold-air/open-liquid sensible and latent exchange with finite temperature/phase limits and appropriate existing bulk methods, and distinguish frozen surface vs unfrozen water. Retain warm case. The observed domain peak wind 77.787m/s warrants a bounded plausibility diagnosis if persistent, not a new circulation search.

Recommended next implementation packages

Generalize current V1 physical coverage first: persistent natural water connections, coarse land/groundwater owners, real full-area precipitation allocation and independent coarse weather grid; map by area/geometry and use physical activity, not camera. Preserve finite pending amounts, stable IDs, common clock, snapshots and new V1 persistence; no legacy migration requirement. Progress from a complete catchment to neighboring catchments, not another selected pair.
Use this coverage to complete actual above-bank regional flooding and recession, connected lake/ocean/cave/spring contacts, automatic local rapid custody/return, and cold surface exchange. Reuse Wflow/FluxCell/CFE/Weather3D/CliMA/COARE donors, no broad solver replacement or additional standalone campaign. Fix actual unsupported contacts, not artificial gate success.
Generalize current-geometry edits, derived queries and nav hazard publication; render all relevant visible water including repaired channels/basins, continue actual sediment/erosion and MeanderPy bank migration/deposition and cutoffs. Keep visual detail independent of physical ownership. Complete coherent normal gameplay.
Complete the existing M5 representative combined 100km severe storm/recession, rendered 512km at 8x with meaningful simultaneous coverage/actors, and 4,000km macro plus active regions; measure inclusive work, frame/debt/memory and actual counts. Avoid premature 32x tuning, repeated old regressions and repeated identical tiny smoke trials. Record exact status and failures. Continue all authorized milestones without new user approval for routine engineering. Escalate only fundamental dependency/requirement blockers.

See technical plan, execution protocol, progress, and M1, M2, M3 evidence. Worker/orchestrator remain owners of active progress and implementation. No changed runtime, new solver, clock, scope or fixed tuning settings authorized by this review.

environmental-foundation-v1.title: Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation-first plan
environmental-foundation-v1.content:
Environmental Foundation V1 — implementation-first plan
26 November 2026. The user agreed to the implementation-first direction: choose evidence-backed upstream numerical implementations, stop prolonged standalone comparative campaigns, and create a concrete continuation plan. This is the selected provisional design baseline, not a declaration that an integrated solver or the performance target has passed. It supersedes the research-first sequencing of water-first qualification; preserve that document and pressure-test evidence, upstream water evidence, reuse decision, formation decision, and requirements. No runtime source changed by this document. The user subsequently authorized full replacement implementation in Codex on 26 November 2026; see execution protocol and the current task scope. Actual runtime implementation has not started by virtue of this documentation change.
1. Deliverable and scope
Deliver a normal playable Godot fresh-world foundation with aged realistic-stylized terrain, distinct curved rivers and meaningful tributaries, finite lakes/ocean, land/soil and groundwater, causal rain/evaporation/heat/wind, connected flooding and recession, local interactive water, slow erosion/migration and real attractive volumetric clouds. Include persistent current geometry and edits, cheap native gameplay field queries and navigation-hazard invalidation. Scale by geography and actual work, not camera visibility; a 100×100 km storm, offscreen changes and a 4,000 km macro configuration are required scale evidence, not optional presentation. Full 100k+ population, complete ecology, all liquid families, advanced abilities and final art content are later dependent scopes; retain their contracts, don’t claim them complete or create irreversible limits. Basic groundwater/cave contacts, finite ocean and cold-phase water cycle are required environmental closure cases, not optional infinite sources.
One primary implementation per role. Ordinary small correctness fixtures, source equivalence and profiling occur while delivering features. No parallel full solver implementations, bespoke PDE engine, reimplementation of vendor test catalogs, revival of LandscapeChannels, or reuse preference for failed native environment mechanisms. Existing Godot/Jolt, Zylann, useful terrain editing, coordinates and integration boundaries may be retained. Preserve legacy artifacts and unpublished work; fresh-world policy is not a migration mandate.
2. Dependency and numerical reuse manifest
Pins are previously inspected source snapshots, not necessarily latest releases or a transitive license approval. Preserve notices and independently check selected files/build dependencies before incorporation. Prefer original callable kernels over copying a whole application; native ports must preserve the upstream numerical method. Record the exact upstream files used and deviations. Do not embed unapproved GPL/AGPL code.











































































RolePrimary source and pinReuse / integration boundaryGeneration / ageGeoGenesis, MITRust single-shot simulation and geology/age/erosion. Small C ABI/export if needed; no second full mutable world. Drainage-area incision versus climate-derived actual discharge requires calibrated adaptation, not a claim that existing code already uses Q for all erosion.Landforms/initial river geometryPWG, MITMain river network/geometry, channel profiles, selected landform functions, deterministic constrained refinement. Do not import viewer or forced joins/8m creek cap.Current solidsZylann, existing pinSparse editable SDF/material, streaming and mesh/collision. Verify actual checkout identity; no duplicate voxel engine.Regional hydraulicsWflow, MITSigned local-inertial flow, stage/area/perimeter lookup, suitable reservoir/groundwater methods. Use actual upstream routines, preserving numerical formulation and stable stepping constraints. Adapt topology/geometry and finite transfer boundaries; reject stock common-stage floodplain and negative-stock clipping. Not a stock turnkey Wflow installation.Root zone/runoffNOAA CFE, Apache-2.0Native C infiltration, root-zone storage, realized ET, lateral/runoff delay. Existing adapter only if narrow and correct. Spatial aquifer owns recharge; CFE conceptual groundwater must be removed/reconciled, not duplicated. Preserve all queue masses and correct units.GroundwaterWflow pin aboveUnconfined saturated thickness, harmonic conductance, finite head/storage and river/spring contact. Use source units and suitable stable timestep; no external constant head creating water without a named inventory. Cavities are separate physical compartments, not a duplicate aquifer.Rapid/detail surfaceFluxCell, MITUpstream MUSCL-Hancock/HLLC, CPU reference and bounded GPU or native path. Use exact scoped results in SRC-WATER-UPSTREAM, not a full suite or target GPU pass. GPU bed update keeps depth; solid mask is fixed; negative sparse source rejected. Explicit withdrawal, safe topology changes and finite parent exchange needed. No dense global grid.Channel migrationMeanderPy, Apache-2.0Curvature/upstream weighting, cutoff and resampling, bounded slow evolution in suitable alluvial channels. Actual discharge/shear/material forcing and physical sediment/geometry edits required; stock migration is not directly flow-driven. O(N) exponential recurrence permissible with constant weighting coefficient, preserving original padding/spacing; no plotting/runtime history package.CirculationWeather3D, MIT sourceReduced hydrostatic/anelastic C-grid core, momentum, hydrostatic diagnostics, vertical continuity, barotropic correction. Do not import full WebGPU app, Earth climatology, default moisture sources or its soil model. Actual native port and conservative coupling are significant work.Transport and cloud phaseconservative MC/TVD and CliMA 0M, Apache-2.0Conservative flux-limited horizontal and vertical water/energy transport; scalar bulk condensation/precipitation/evaporation tendencies, cold phase, latent heat. 0M alone is instantaneous precipitation removal; explicitly own falling water/snow and cap evaporation/condensation by available mass and saturation. No Julia runtime by default.Surface energyCOARE 3.6, MITAir-water bulk exchange coefficient/flux calculation; use actual accepted ET/evaporation and heat transfer, appropriate land/lake calibration, finite thermal inventories. No prescribed ocean temperature reset.Cloud renderingSunshineClouds2, MITActual Godot compositor/volumetric rendering. Reduce stock 300 ray/32 lighting step limits; data-driven discrete shapes, multi-altitude forms, depth compositing and temporal history. No duplicated physical weather.NavigationHPA/DHPA and existing local Recast/Detour directionNot a population rewrite in V1. Publish passability, depth/velocity, door/barrier and geometry revisions for later local paths/hierarchical summaries. Do not require world-wide metre occupancy.
Fallbacks are not parallel implementations. SFINCS scientific reference (GPL-3.0, embedding not approved), ADCIRC (LGPL review and topology issues), mizuRoute (ordinary downstream only) remain available only if primary fails a named requirement. ERF warm-rain and other archived atmospheric models are reference/fallback only. A new technology search must be driven by a specific demonstrated blocker, not routine development.
3. Final source-level reuse review
Wflow: surface_process.jl takes prior discharge, two stages, face water depth, area, hydraulic radius, path length, squared Manning roughness, Froude limit and dt. Signed semi-implicit friction law is directly separable. Floodplain profile functions provide depth/flow area/wetted perimeter/storage inversion. Groundwater and river-groundwater contact are narrow donors. Its regional storage update merges river and floodplain to common stage and records negative corrections after clipping; do not preserve these semantics. Stable timestep is a depth/length bound for its discretization, not proof for new subgrid graph. Use existing update loops where compatible; independent compartments, connected face geometry, simultaneous finite transfer acceptance, topology repair and subgrid stability are genuine integration changes. A Froude cap cannot be used to suppress a rapid flood. Earlier independent probe shows dry-dam front error about 54% for simplified local inertia. Keep it for ordinary low-Froude flows; promote or use a qualified shock-capable representation when needed.
Weather3D: pe.wgsl computes hydrostatic and vertical mass continuity; momentum and nonconservative scalar transport are in pe_stage. pe.js projects each of three RK stages, with variable-column-mass iterations using direct DFT/inverse transforms and Thomas solve. For square 125²/250² grid, one direct forward/inverse pair per each of three stages is 6*N³ = 11,718,750 / 93,750,000 inner summation terms per full timestep, excluding iterations and column work. Do not port direct DFT literally. Reuse an established permissively licensed fast transform/linear-algebra backend suitable for the chosen boundary conditions (audit existing dependencies first), and retain variable-coefficient correction and residual control where needed. Do not assume periodic-x/closed-y fits a bounded world; choose saved boundary policy and explicit fluxes, e.g. compatible no-normal-flow boundaries with matching transform/solver, or a deliberately periodic world. Reference profiles, Earth-dependent nudging and independent soil/moisture/SST forcing cannot create water/energy; disable or replace with accounted game forcing. Conservative face transport must use the same dry-air mass flux, include vertical face transfers and consistent latent/sensible energy. This is a reduced-model port, not a turnkey atmosphere. Do not present dropping pressure correction or clamping negative humidity as an optimization pass.
4. Shared physical representation

Whole-world metric coordinates (checked wide integer identity; local float offsets), independent solver lattices. Initial configurable macro geography ~4km for 4,000km; 16km addressing pages, not solver boundaries; 32km atmosphere with 8 layers as initial cost-conscious starting point, local/nested 16km or smaller where justified. Pilot smaller domain with appropriate resolution, not a single uniform 32km cell presented as a storm.
Aged geometry produces persistent feature IDs, channel polylines/splines and true length, bed/bank profiles, cross sections, crest/sill elevations, compartments/outlet connectivity, V(stage), wet area and face conveyance, material/soil/roughness/cover, cave contacts. Fine realization and all derived tables agree with the same recipe+edits. No render-stage-driven recarving, no global metre DEM/SDF scans. Regional fine sampling only where required; keep hydrographic topology correct across page boundaries. Sparse channel density around 0.1 km/km² of land and average 2km hydraulic segments are proposed configurable starting settings, not arbitrary minimum/maximum or user-approved immutable counts. Retain meaningful 1m creeks, unbounded meaningful river widths, natural confluences, beautiful curved planform; omitted minor drainage contributes actual catchment runoff and can produce local wetness.
Surface authoritative quantities: volume, stage derived from current geometry, signed flow/momentum as required by selected method, thermal and relevant constituent mass. Soil owns actual storage and runoff queue; spatial groundwater owns aquifer head/storage; ocean is finite. Air owns dry-air convention, temperature/energy, wind/pressure, vapor/condensate/falling precipitation. Geometry has a revision; each field snapshot has coverage/precision/time, not an alternative physical owner. No per-renderer state as physical truth.
At a common accepted model interval: air supplies integrated precipitation; partition once by receiving area and geometry; soil yields runoff/recharge; surface accepts flow and withdrawals; actual ET/open-water evaporation/heat return once; record finite pending transfers until consumed. Conservative sums, nonnegative donor amounts, and overlap in space/time. Update material only from accumulated real erosion/deposition; refresh affected geometry/navigation and conserve water when volume changes. Refinement replaces parent authority for represented volume, and coarsening reconciles actual stock/tracer/heat and timing; no double counting. Trigger by physical state or interactions, not camera. Renderer reads snapshots only.

5. Clocks and engineering cost envelope
Retain configurable 600s/day, 60 days/year calendar. Do not require 144 physical seconds per game-second for every physical process simply to match an Earth day. Initial playable test setting: common water/atmosphere physical clock of 1 physical second per simulated game-second, with separately saved calendar/solar forcing. Caleb confirmed 1:1 for the initial testing, an 8× wall-clock gameplay baseline and a 32× gameplay stretch target. The tested physical mapping and the gameplay-speed setting are independent. Production acceptance still requires the integrated measurements below. At 8x simulation a 20 physical-second release lasts 2.5 real seconds at alpha1, 0.208s at alpha12, 0.0174s at alpha144. Weather movement, water cycle, runoff queues and season pacing must be coherent under the declared clock; no pretending this is an Earth-time 24h day, no independent camera clock. If pacing is too slow, adjust a declared world/physical policy with measured cost, not silent dt compression. Historical alpha144 remains a sensitivity comparator.
Arithmetic from recorded synthetic EPYC probes and upstream claim, not target performance: 50% land over 16Mkm² ×0.1km/km² /2km =400k reaches; 64B/reach illustrative 24.4MiB before curves, edges, scratch, saves. At 29.8ns/update, one full update is 11.92ms; at hypothetical stable dt300 physical seconds, alpha1/12/144 =0.040/0.477/5.722 aggregate CPU-ms/game-s. At dt60s =0.199/2.384/28.608. This does not establish actual graph or Wflow update cost/stability. A 100x100km storm with 250m cells previously measured synthetic 45.92 CPU-ms/game-s at alpha144 -> .319 at alpha1; 1km .761 ->.0053, not proof of comparable fidelity. 32/16km atmosphere transport+column probes .77/4.95 at alpha144 -> .0053/.0344 at alpha1; dynamics not included. Actual cadence constrained by geometry, dynamics and accuracy. Do not infer combined budget from these estimates. 256² at 1m, dt=.05s, 8x at alpha1 needs 10.49M cell updates/s, nominal .287 GPU-ms/frame at FluxCell’s author-reported 610M/s; at alpha144 41.26ms/frame, before integration. Do not use high-resolution solver everywhere. Budget from actual complete workload and peak service cost, not divided by worker count.
Reference target: Ryzen 7 3700X, RTX2070 SUPER, 32GB, 1080p/60fps, sustained 8x without growing debt (future 32–64x aspiration). No such integrated result is claimed. Historical aggregate environment CPU target 25ms/game-s, 512MiB steady, 768MiB autosave, 1GiB replacement, .5ms water GPU/frame and 32MiB water VRAM are comparison targets, not newly approved rigid subsystem allocations. Broad flood/edits, memory, CPU/GPU/frame, query and publication cost and save debt included. Report peak latency and complete work. Choose coarse connected storage and multirate scheduling consistent with actual transfer clocks, not just arbitrary reduced cadence or fine region caps.
6. One release in six implementation milestones
Proceed to the next milestone when the implemented output is usable and its directly relevant acceptance criteria are met. These are delivery milestones, not a separate exploratory research campaign. Reuse upstream checks and the same one connected world; no endless independent benchmark phase. If a hard failure occurs, record the smallest specific issue, fix the integration when bounded, or stop that component and reconsider the dependency.
M0 — Prepare and pin
Inspect actual worktree, build instructions, existing terrain API, scheduler, saves, branch status and unpublished changes. Create isolated reviewed implementation branch/worktree from appropriate code head and import canonical Brain decisions; don’t base runtime work on docs alone without checking differences. Freeze dependency manifest, source/license notices, units/clock, world seed and scenario/tolerance definitions. Runtime scope is authorized by the user on 26 November 2026; synchronize the active task and instructions into the actual implementation checkout. Don’t delete legacy data or overwrite another writer. Deliver reproducible build and start fresh-world policy.
M1 — One aged editable world
Integrate GeoGenesis core, selected PWG geometry/morphology and existing Zylann. Form macro geography, age at chosen years, export final original bed/material/climate/drainage (not filled diagnostic water stock), build feature-first channel/basin geometry, initialize finite stock later. Generate visible small valley with 1m tributary, curved river, lake, closed depression, mountains and editable land; test adjacent seams and matching hydraulic curves from same solids. Use real authored/generated geometry, not fixture-only solver. Deliver visible terrain, world age/density/shape configuration, finite geometry summaries and macro 4,000km count/bytes/startup census without full fine generation. If fine tributaries do not respect parent outlet, fix recipe before adding water.
M2 — Water replacement
Integrate upstream Wflow numerical routines, connected independently staged subgrid compartments, finite volume exchange; CFE native soil/runoff, finite Wflow-derived groundwater/springs and coastal/ocean inventory. Ordinary reach+flood storage first; use FluxCell only for needed rapid detailed patches and demonstrate conservative authority transfer and actual geometry/withdrawal updates. Do not port full Julia stack or rebuild old graph. Render real stage-clipped water, query depth/current cheaply, include dams/weirs and narrow channel controls. Meter rainfall as a temporary explicit forcing fixture, not production weather. Deliver playable filling, draining, extraction, rainfall/runoff, backwater, protected settlement, gate opening/reversal, wet excavation, caves and save/reload with offscreen progression. No double-stock, infinite source, ghost water across sealed barrier or widespread fine-grid requirement. If geometry/positivity/stability work turns Wflow into a new general-purpose solver, stop and reconsider regional dependency; do not hide it in adapters. If rapid-flow area exceeds FluxCell budget, record missing regional capability, don’t clamp away physically consequential floods.
M3 — Live coupled weather
Implement Weather3D reduced numerical core on CPU-compatible packed fields using established pressure backend, conservative MC/TVD fluxes, selected CliMA bulk phase and finite falling rain/snow, COARE-informed exchange and surface heat capacity. Generate actual wind/rain responses to topography, temperature, humidity, seasons and water; connect CFE/surface/GW, remove temporary rain driver from normal path. Cloud physics snapshot supplies base/top, condensate, types and movement. Require mass and simplified energy accounting of all physical exchanges and explicit boundary/solar energy, stable circulation with meaningful wet/dry and mountain rain-shadow behavior, no arbitrary rainfall source or doubled ET. Drought and rewetting must affect both sides. Provide field queries for gameplay independent of renderer. If the native reduced dynamics port becomes a rewrite or cannot maintain stability/physical finite coupling without large compute, return the specific blocker instead of adding a heavyweight atmosphere.
M4 — Erosion and visual world
Reuse GeoGenesis bed/hillslope/material methods where applicable and MeanderPy slow alluvial migration/cutoffs, driven by actual accumulated flow/shear, sediment, wind, rainfall and material/vegetation resistance; protected hard/engineered banks constrain movement. Separate fast stage/wetted width from slow physical bed/centerline changes. Apply bounded persistent solid edits and repair water and relevant environmental summaries; cutoffs retain finite stock and connectivity, not cosmetic curves. Integrate SunshineClouds2 real volumetric compositor: start quarter-linear resolution 480x270 at 1080p, 24–48 primary samples, low lighting sample count, early-out/empty-space skipping and depth-aware temporal reconstruction. Default stock settings not accepted. Shape driven by persistent meteorological formations, reuse 3D density shapes where supported, dynamic sunlight, beautiful open-sky gaps when weather permits. Do not build second weather simulator or fixed baked sun shading. Deliver attractive normal gameplay view below/above/inside clouds, moving sun/camera, storm, clean curved streams and changing water stage/terrain. Keep measured frame/VRAM costs, not screenshot-only pass.
M5 — Complete release evidence and scale
Use the same environment-only implementation to run a connected valley, representative 100x100km severe storm/recession and 4,000km macro with multiple simultaneous active environmental regions and sparse terrain/solver residency. Intermediate scales only when useful; use compatible cached inputs. No colony/actor/navigation workload. Do not equate idle macro load with a fully active world. Include offscreen edits, dams, dry/wet, finite snow/ice and heat, cave/ocean/groundwater exchange, representative environmental depth/velocity/hazard queries (no navigation consumer work), paced save/reload and actual rendered host. Report accepted finite residuals, water levels/arrival/hazard/extent against simple analytical or existing fine reference, no false closed-barrier crossing. Choose gameplay-relevant error thresholds before work; historical 5cm/10%/IoU0.9 are proposed fixture starting tolerances not universal scientific accuracy or new accepted requirements. Record exact source/binary/config and inclusive CPU/GPU/RAM/debt/p95/p99/frame/latency, generation/age separately, actual visible captures. Prove no global scan or full fine promotion. Record actual success/failure and unresolved features; only promote validated capabilities and leave future scale/ECS/ecology/other-liquid work open. Prefer a smaller truthful functioning release with named open failures to falsely labeling 4,000km/8x production-ready.
7. Stop conditions and reporting
No competing full solver builds, blanket dependency upgrades, old water optimization, unapproved license, invented source implementation, or numerical redesign masquerading as integration. Preserve tests as ordinary development, not months of independent qualification. When a hard requirement fails, show exact source/fixture/profile, why reuse cannot solve it cheaply, and the smallest viable replacement/contract change; obtain approval if changing fundamental gameplay, clocks or dependency/license. Do not hide unresolved full hydraulic, pressure, rendering or population costs. No separate repeated paper search unless a concrete blocker. Commit bounded code+evidence on reviewable branch, update canonical Brain systems, candidate dispositions and traceability. Never edit generated website repo; run atlas generation/check/tests and use the cached local publication procedure in Brain workflow; no routine private Actions builds. This plan makes actual technology choices provisional, not a claim of new performance or integration validation.
8. User-approved full replacement execution
The user approved the implementation-first design and all M1–M5 delivery work on 26 November 2026. The active work is full replacement, not an optional branch of the old environment system. Follow the execution protocol for orchestration, continuous progress and public Brain publication. No milestone requires another user permission unless it exposes a fundamental decision or real blocker. M0 is preparation, not a further research gate. Minimal targeted verification is required for the changed path only; do not reproduce comprehensive legacy compatibility or vendor validation. Preserve truthful status, hard physical invariants, representative scale evidence and repository safety. Remove or disconnect obsolete environmental paths where the replacement is ready, without deleting unrelated assets, saves or unpublished changes. Proposed tunable settings remain configurable; routine reversible engineering decisions are delegated. No measured performance or runtime implementation is established by this authorization.
9. Controlling user scope correction — 27 November 2026
Follow the concrete environment-only A–F implementation plan before remaining milestone work. One reusable development baseline for Codex, native/headless preferred as appropriate, at most one active Godot environmental development scene and no UI requirement. Fast dependency-aware builds and cached recipes/checkpoints. Then exceptionally smooth real 3D continent-to-local terrain zoom, prioritizing existing Zylann, bounded residency and minimal derived far representation only when needed. Finish connected water, weather, terrain evolution, and representative environmental-only qualification. No colonists, actor/settlement/navigation integration, tests, tuning or compatibility work until separate later scope. The existing physical design, selected dependencies and accepted 1:1 clock remain. Fundamental architecture decisions are retained by the user and planning chat, not delegated to Codex. This scope overrides conflicting older milestone delivery requirements, not physical invariants or evidence. 8x environment-only and 60 FPS reference goals remain, 32x stretch deferred. No new implementation or validation claim.
10. Final implementation continuation, 27 November 2026
The user approved a fresh main local orchestration chat and two actual local worker chats for the remaining V1 completion work. The active plan’s completion campaign and reusable demonstrations and execution protocol now govern sequencing and test delivery. Preserve this technical plan’s physical requirements and selected numerical reuse; do not restart completed work. Configurable actual geological-age replay, real high-quality fast continent-to-ground streaming/LOD, reusable water, weather/atlas, erosion and integrated live-world scenarios are required through the single existing runner. No mandatory new UI or scene. Close actual missing capabilities, then verify representative integrated cases. All colony/navigation/settlement work remains excluded.

formation-comparison.title: World formation comparison and remaining terrain scope
formation-comparison.content:
World formation comparison and remaining terrain scope
Source review: 25 November 2026. Both candidates MIT. Existing provisional GeoGenesis selection remains subject to comparison; recommend Procedural World Generation first in the surface-formation comparison because the user values the demonstrated geographic quality. Neither is validated on target hardware. No engine code modified.
Actual scope























































CapabilityGeoGenesisProcedural World GenerationSurface geographyTectonic relief, crust/isostasy, landform stamps and ageTectonic relief, staged landform passes, LEM and refined terrainGeological timePersistent coupled simulation, age in years, replayIterated uplift/incision/diffusion with time step in years; age-conditioned parameters, staged buildReliefPlateaus, mesas, ranges, rifts, faults, calderas, peaksTerraces, mesas, buttes, escarpments, coastal cliffs, sea stacks, volcanism, karst and glacial/coastal landformsGeology/materialsRock properties, strata, age, dip, fault offset, soil/sediment, mineral prospectivityErodibility, geological provinces, simplified strata/landform and biome layersDrainageD8/MFD, depression fill, climate-derived flow; needs finer realizationExplicit reach graph, lakes, meanders, deltas, local trunk/creek growth and CPU terrain detailOutputHeightfield, maps, 3D surface mesh, geology descriptorsHeightfield, typed-array fields, feature graphs, CDLOD surface and visual effectsTrue volumetric terrainNot suppliedNot suppliedLive finite gameplay hydrology/weatherNot suppliedNot suppliedNative integrationDependency-light Rust core, export/ABI adapter neededTypeScript numerical core and headless benchmark; export/native port of proven functions to qualify
GeoGenesis source: initial formation, age driver, geology, mineral scoring. PWG source: pipeline, LEM, age config, landforms, arid, cliffs, hydrology, creeks, creek tests.
Recommendation: compare whole formation outputs, not stack two full generators. PWG’s explicit landform diversity and local creek implementation may avoid significant custom engineering. GeoGenesis is better aligned with chronological coupled age and material inventories. A beautiful demo does not by itself establish native runtime speed, physically correct finite water, or 3D geology. PWG’s rendering and visual embellishment should not be mistaken for the physical terrain. If PWG wins, consider only needed compatible GeoGenesis rock/stratigraphy and geological-process kernels, not a second world owner. If GeoGenesis wins, borrow PWG’s targeted landform/creek/geometry routines rather than running PWG’s entire macro pipeline afterward.
Bounded selection gate

Run both pinned upstream generators headlessly using the same physical world width and comparable output resolution/land fraction/climate settings. Use a small reproducible seed set representing humid mountainous islands, dry plateau/canyon terrain and volcanic or glacial terrain. Seeds need not map to identical geography across different algorithms. Inspect final exported elevation, not renderer exaggeration, and measure cold macro generation, aging/evolution, refinement/export and peak working memory separately. GeoGenesis’s author timings are not a direct comparison; PWG has a source-inspected benchmark entry point.
Compare actual plateau/cliff profiles, river continuity, lake/outlet connectivity, relief variation, geology/material information, age controls and age-dependent changes. Freeze tolerances and visual evaluation views before testing. Report which landforms are process-driven vs explicit stamps; both are legitimate if coherent and configurable.
Test actual natural fine river/creek realization, including 1 m feature geometry where representable, cross-page continuity, closed basins, deterministic re-generation and no view-dependent physical geometry. Existing creek tests are useful starting evidence, not our validation. A fixed height callback and persistent parent routing/finite inventory contracts are mandatory.
Only after upstream evidence, compare native interop costs and one bounded Godot/Zylann view with true caves and materials. Select one source. Do not start a large port or new framework to make either candidate fit. Probe 4,000 km coarse scaling with no dense fine allocations. Distinguish failed/partial/accepted results.

Additional scope retained from the environmental plan
These items are not made unnecessary by selecting a formation engine. They remain required or explicitly phased in existing records.




























































DomainStill neededCanonical owner/requirementTrue 3D geologyCaves, overhangs, tunnels, coherent underground strata/materials, finite deposits; Zylann SDF and sparse editsQ-VOLUME, REQ-EDITSurface geometryStable channels/banks, lakes, basin capacity, dams, cross-page routing and local editsCON-TERRAIN, Q-REFINESoil and groundwaterActual infiltration, evapotranspiration, soil stores, aquifers, springs and cave exchanges; CFE remains provisional land kernelSYS-LAND, SYS-GW, OPT-CFEDynamic finite hydraulicsRivers/lakes/ocean, local controls, broad flood/recession, accepted volume transportREQ-WATER, REQ-FLOOD, Q-FLOODLiquidsBasic contamination and additional liquid families; sparse transport and meaningful effectsREQ-LIQUID, REQ-CONTAMWeatherWind/temperature/moisture circulation, actual evaporation, cloud transport and precipitation, seasonal forcing; ERF Kessler only a cloud donorQ-ATMOS, OPT-ERFLive erosion and sedimentActual runoff/discharge/wind/material activity causes later terrain evolution, including deposition and soil fertility; not wholesale regenerating an inhabited worldSYS-EROSION, CON-SEDIMENT, Q-EROSIONEcologyPersistent vegetation, succession, fauna, feedback to infiltration/ET/erosion, farming and resourcesREQ-ECOCurrents and visualsRiver velocities, wind-driven water currents, waves, atmosphere/cloud presentation, coherent material/foliage renderingSYS-CURRENTS, REQ-VISUALGameplay and scaleECS, hierarchical travel and crowd movement, offscreen work, mining, cultivation edits, common time/scheduling, save/reload and measurementsREQ-PEOPLE, REQ-NAV, REQ-FANTASY, REQ-PERSIST, REQ-BUDGET
Do not conflate deferred qualification with deleted requirements. The next experiment chooses a formation source and establishes its geometry handoff; subsequent finite water, weather, ecology and entity qualification remain unchanged.
User review: stream scale, landforms and geology
User finds PWG’s small-stream appearance unconvincing, particularly the 8 m cap, but values explicit landform/terracing algorithms and the absence of equivalent wind erosion and mineral deposit support is a concern. Source follow-up: the 8 m cap is only in small-stream geometry, not macro river sizing. River density and meandering controls exist; creek width/depth caps and several growth rules are hardcoded. At 4 km macro spacing the existing channel-head area floor is 40 km². The existing split is a rendering-oriented approximation; Breachborn needs one coherent feature hierarchy with configurable hydraulic geometry, catchment/mean or bankfull discharge, local slope/material and physical units. Do not infer live water volume from carved width. A fixed minimum or maximum is not a physical stream-order rule. Do not accept forced joins/cell-boundary artifacts or visual-only creek ribbons as physical topology.
Provisional engineering preference: retain GeoGenesis as the age/material baseline, qualify PWG’s strongest explicit terracing/landform and main-network/geometry kernels as targeted donors, and keep PWG full formation as the comparison challenger. This reflects the user’s newly expressed priorities and the source-confirmed richer geological process model. If PWG’s headless geometry, costs and coherent age/material adapter win the existing gate, choose PWG instead. Avoid both full formation pipelines in one world and avoid duplicating existing erosion. Prefer a single geology/terrain owner with optional generation-time landform processes and runtime forcing-driven material changes.
Add to the comparative acceptance gate: (1) creek/trunk/river scale continuity across macro spacing and density, natural morphology without inappropriate forced junctions, configurable widths/depths, and reference bankfull dimensions distinct from dynamic wetted dimensions; (2) bare versus vegetated/arid wind erosion, finite loose-material budget, downwind deposition and recorded dust/export; test physical scale and actual wind fields rather than accepting the donor’s cell-count transport; (3) reproducible rock strata and resource prospectivity, with finite local 3D mineable resource realization a separate Q-VOLUME gate; (4) cliffs/terraces/canyons rendered from the same final solid geometry as hydraulics and navigation, with natural drainage preserved after landform passes. See candidate records for exact pinned source evidence. No benchmark or user-approved final selection.
Coupled compatibility gate
Status: proposed gate, not passed. The current source review confirms extensible formation processes and useful surface geometry algorithms. No full live hydraulic, groundwater or atmosphere implementation has been qualified against either formation candidate. Keep the formation comparison open until the following interface and coupled checks have evidence:

































BoundaryRequired contract and discriminating checkFormation / added landformVersioned metric terrain/material recipe, stable deterministic feature identities; add a terrace/cliff, depression or crater; refresh drainage/outlets, geological properties and terrain summaries after mutation.Surface waterGeometry-derived connected storage partitions, stage-volume/area, bed/bank/saddle/face/control geometry, finite ocean/lake/river inventories, signed accepted fluxes. A natural river, two basins, barrier and dam edit show conserved transfer, correct spill, arrival and recession.Soil / groundwaterFinite soil/recharge/spring/underground exchanges and actual cave contacts; no duplicate groundwater store when using a conceptual land kernel.AtmosphereGeometry and surface properties mapped conservatively to the selected coarse atmospheric grid, wind/thermal gradients, vapor/cloud transport and precipitation. Compare mountain rain shadow, wet/dry land and ocean exchange; not a static climate map.Coupled live evolutionActual terrestrial evaporation removes water, credits vapor, transports it downwind, condenses and rains; rainfall partitions once to land/open water, runoff moves downstream and changes storage; erosion/deposition uses accepted forcing and commits geometry changes. Test water and material closure, causal timing and geometry changes.Scale / visualAll above remain meaningful offscreen and after save/reload/promotion. No whole-map fine terrain admission. Measure inclusive CPU/GPU/memory and debt with actual Godot presentation, 100 x 100 km severe storm, and 4,000 km logical-domain scale probes. Freeze error/performance criteria before tests.
The first gate is deliberately a small connected case, not full production integration or literal molecular/3D CFD. Independent solver resolution and cadence remain allowed if conservation, meaningful outcomes, feedback and local refinement are established. Additional liquid families, contamination, currents, ecology, seasonal/weather range and full scale still require subsequent qualification under existing requirements. If a shortlisted solver requires incompatible geometry or unbounded fine work, change that solver/representation before locking the stack; do not discard required water or weather behavior.

questions/q-atmos.title: Which lightweight atmosphere and transport?
questions/q-atmos.content:
Which lightweight atmosphere and transport?
Compare reduced atmosphere methods and permissive numerical donors. Demonstrate wind/thermal gradients, downwind moisture, condensation/rain, actual ET, seasons and large storm under budget. Verify cloud rendering consumes same fields and later snow/currents/vegetation interfaces.
Complementary pressure review
Weather3D reduced dynamics lead, CliMT and JCM independent physics, CliMA 0M finite phase adaptation, COARE bulk coupling. MC/TVD preferred over upwind-only in independent 720km tracer probe; dynamic atmosphere remains unqualified. True volumetric clouds mandatory per REQ-VISUAL. Review.
Implementation-first selection (26 November 2026)
Use reduced Weather3D hydrostatic/anelastic C-grid dynamics as primary donor, with compatible established pressure solver, conservative MC/TVD finite transports, CliMA bulk phase and COARE-derived exchanges. Environmental Foundation V1 records exact source pin and adaptation boundaries. No stock atmosphere or full validation claimed; this question stays open for implementation evidence. No new competing atmosphere campaigns.

questions/q-erosion.title: Which erosion methods can run during play?
questions/q-erosion.content:
Which erosion methods can run during play?
Compare stream-power/hillslope methods and suitable sediment accounting. Feed actual runoff/discharge, soil/material properties and vegetation; test erosion/deposition and terrain revision without erasing player construction or rebuilding entire map.
Formation/runtime forcing comparison (26 November 2026)
See GeoGenesis source correction and formation clarification. First verify the upstream implicit area-based and discharge-aware geological laws under wet/dry and varying-discharge controls, including threshold effects. A representative statistical climate/runoff forcing is appropriate for prehistory; live erosion must use actual accepted flows/erosive exposure and material resistance. Reuse established erosion/deposition implementations (GeoGenesis, Wflow sediment candidate where appropriate, Landlab as reference) rather than duplicate overlapping erosion laws. Validate sustained erosion/deposition, local sediment accounting, altered channels and dam/cave geometry, navigation revision and no removal of construction by whole-world regeneration. Scope each physical process and timescale separately.
Stylized dynamic channel migration (26 November 2026)
MeanderPy is a newly source-screened permissive kinematic channel-migration donor. Evaluate its curvature/upstream-weighted law and cutoff/centerline resampling before new implementation. Stock migration does not directly include flow velocity/discharge and is not a finite hydraulic or terrain/material solver; qualify modulation by actual accumulated flow/shear, material and vegetation resistance, coherent erosion/deposition and topology updates. Restrict to suitable alluvial reaches; canyon/bedrock channels should not wander unrealistically. Preserve construction and water custody during migration/cutoffs. No runtime adoption.

questions/q-flood.title: Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?
questions/q-flood.content:
Which scalable hydraulic algorithm?
Qualify signed head law, wet/dry, backwater, control/levee, downstream arrival, storage curves and dynamic geometry. Compare whole-island storm and two-basin/levee cases against finer reference with declared error and memory/throughput. No wholesale local refinement. Use historical SWMM/CaMa failures as negative evidence.
Numerical source screen
Landlab OverlandFlow is an independently implemented local-inertial raster reference. NOAA t-route diffusive routing exposes a C binding and cross-section preparation; the whole solver has module-global state. Neither qualifies as a turnkey sparse subgrid engine. Compare two practical coarse algorithms: a signed quasi-steady diffusive-wave head law using stage-dependent conductance versus a local-inertial face-discharge update retaining prior momentum. Use SFINCS/CaMa as algorithm references and independent fine Landlab controls. Start with one conservative stage-volume store per connected partition and explicit saddle/face geometry; both alternatives must handle closed barriers and exact accepted-volume debit/credit. Reject equilibrium-only flow for travel-time tests, unaccounted thin films/floors, or a requirement to promote an entire storm region to metre cells. See spatial qualification. This is a shortlist for tests, not a selected production solver.
Complementary pressure review
Compare mizuRoute IRF ordinary reach delayed flow, Wflow connected low-Froude and FluxCell rapid-flow reference. No old native reuse preference. Independent large-step oscillation despite perfect ledger and 250m storm time-cost probe in review.
Upstream-first replacement gate (26 November 2026)
The next comparison must execute existing upstream implementations before undertaking a new hydraulic port or implementation. Start with Wflow as the broad permissive candidate, SFINCS as independent mature subgrid reference, and FluxCell as rapid-flow candidate. Wflow documentation and floodplain limitations; 2026 SFINCS global flood validation (extent validation, not depth/game performance); FluxCell (MIT, CPU references and GPU implementation). Independently measure actual regional model and detailed solver using identical frozen geometries, inflows, physical clock, accuracy and inclusive cost criteria. Test narrow creeks, closed basins, dam/backwater/reversal, storm/recession, dynamic solid edits and transfers. mizuRoute only if separate ordinary reach routing earns its additional integration complexity. The old integration is negative evidence, not a required implementation baseline. No new solver is accepted by this record.
26 November upstream execution and regional rescreen
New evidence: bounded pinned FluxCell CPU analytical and gate/edit tests passed, but a full suite attempt timed out and GPU performance, mutable masks, withdrawals and multiscale coupling remain open. FluxCell is the provisional first detailed candidate, not the regional answer. Wflow’s actual same-stage storage code, negative-stock clipping and static network initialization mean a direct stock regional flood integration is not accepted. Retain Wflow for land-water evaluation. Add ADCIRC as a leading regional contender against SFINCS; test actual upstream before deciding whether either is usable, including license compatibility and mesh/lookup repair. Do not infer that subgrid or quasi-1D support resolves all scale, conservation or cave problems. Terrain-to-water export and clock selection are architecture gates, not follow-up polish.
Implementation-first selection (26 November 2026)
Use Wflow signed local-inertial and storage/profile numerical methods as primary ordinary regional implementation with independent connected compartments and finite donor transfers; FluxCell for genuinely necessary rapid details. Environmental Foundation V1 describes source reuse and implementation boundaries. Do not develop parallel regional backends. If required adaptation becomes a bespoke engine or fails a hard requirement, report the blocker. Regional solver remains unvalidated; this question stays open for implementation evidence.
